chapters.title: Chapter 460 -460-Upgrading the Holy Grail
paragraphs: [Nameless Omnipotent Treasure]
[Grade]: Primordial Supreme Treasure
[Type]: Auxiliary Material
[Effects]:
It can be used as a material for refining and enhancing other treasures, or as the embryo of a new treasure.
It can specifically raise the grade of any treasure.
Alternatively, the user may refine one of their own Sacred Arts into it, transforming the treasure into a personal artifact with a compatibility rate of up to 100%.
[Note]:
The exact effects depend upon the number of Nameless Omnipotent Treasures used.
The greater the quantity, the higher the grade to which the target treasure may be raised, and the greater the probability of achieving 100% compatibility.
At present, these treasures can raise a single Divine-grade treasure to Primordial Supreme Treasure-grade at most.
[Description]:
As its name suggests, the Nameless Omnipotent Treasure can be used for almost anything.
It may serve as a crafting or fusion material to raise the grade of another treasure.
It may also be used as a treasure embryo to forge a personal artifact uniquely suited to its owner.
It can even replicate one of the user’s Sacred Arts, engraving an identical ability into the artifact and transforming it into an exclusive sacred treasure.
After reading the description and effects of the Nameless Omnipotent Treasure, a golden gleam immediately appeared in Daniel’s eyes.
Its applications were far broader than those of the Vigilance Crystal he had obtained earlier.
More importantly, its enhancement limit reached peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasure level.
That was almost the same grade as the black Divine Spear in his possession.
Daniel had previously been frustrated by his inability to find a way to advance the Voidbound Grail.
Now that he possessed these Nameless Omnipotent Treasures, he finally had an opportunity to upgrade it.
If he successfully advanced the Voidbound Grail, he would possess more than five treasures at Primordial Supreme Treasure-grade or above.
With that thought, Daniel did not hesitate.
He raised his hand and retrieved the Voidbound Grail he had used earlier.
He then exerted a small amount of power and tossed several Nameless Omnipotent Treasures into it.
The two immediately began to fuse.
Like ripples of liquid, the Nameless Omnipotent Treasures smoothly merged into the Voidbound Grail.
However, the grail did not appear to change at all.
It did not even release the slightest flash of unusual light.
After thinking for a moment, Daniel guessed that he had not used enough of them.
He immediately threw all the remaining Nameless Omnipotent Treasures into the grail.
Just like the previous ones, they transformed into watery ripples and rapidly sank into the Voidbound Grail.
Sure enough, the moment the final treasures entered, a system notification rang in his ears.
[Ding! Congratulations, Player. The Voidbound Grail has successfully completed its advancement!]
[Current Grade of the Voidbound Grail: Primordial Supreme Treasure!]
[Ding! This advancement has triggered the amplification effect!]
[Congratulations, Player. You have obtained the peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasure: Voidbound Grail — Treasure Spirit Awakened!]
Several notifications rang out in succession, and a smile immediately appeared on Daniel’s face.
As expected, as long as he possessed enough Nameless Omnipotent Treasures, the Voidbound Grail could be advanced.
What surprised him even more was that the advancement had triggered an amplification effect.
It had directly raised the Voidbound Grail to peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasure level.
It had even awakened a Treasure Spirit.
Daniel immediately began carefully examining the grail in his hand, eager to see how it had changed after advancing.
The upgraded Voidbound Grail had now reached the same grade as his black Divine Spear.
After observing it for only a few moments, Daniel discovered the tremendous changes brought about by its advancement.
"As expected, the Voidbound Grail’s effects have improved by far more than a single level."
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Before its advancement, the Voidbound Grail could affect only treasures at Primordial Law-grade or below.
Now, however, its spatial sealing ability could even influence peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasures.
In other words, the current Voidbound Grail could unconditionally suppress every Divine-grade treasure at peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasure level or below.
Furthermore, no existence beneath high-stage Oracle-grade could break through the spacetime-sealing domain created by the Voidbound Grail.
The upgraded grail had even obtained an additional characteristic—
Impervious to All Laws.
Just like Daniel’s black Divine Spear, it could now resist law-based Sacred Arts released by high-stage Oracle-grade experts.
After its advancement, the Voidbound Grail could truly be regarded as an exceptional supreme treasure.
The large number of Nameless Omnipotent Treasures Daniel had consumed had not been wasted.
After finishing his inspection of all his gains, Daniel did not linger.
He returned directly to the Emperor-class sacred vessel and continued on his journey.
Somewhere within a hidden corner of the universe—
"Damn it! That man is far too powerful. What are we supposed to do now?"
Daniel’s battle against the four mysterious experts had already been secretly witnessed by every powerhouse who had yet to make a move.
They were deeply wary of the combat strength Daniel had displayed.
After all, the experts who had attacked him were roughly equal to them in strength.
Every one of them had been a high-stage Oracle-grade powerhouse from the future of a different universe.
They were high-stage Oracle-grade experts!
Each of them had once been invincible within their own universe.
They had dominated entire eras, forcing whole star systems to bow beneath their feet.
They were overlords who ruled vast galaxies.
And there had not been only one expert of that level among Daniel’s attackers.
Four had attacked him simultaneously.
Daniel, on the other hand, had been completely alone.
Admittedly, all four high-stage Oracle-grade experts had been suppressed by the Great Dao rules of this plane.
Their strength had been restricted to Divine-grade, preventing them from displaying their true cultivation.
But wasn’t Daniel also a Divine-grade expert?
Logically speaking, with everyone standing at the same level, Daniel should never have been capable of defeating the side with the overwhelming numerical advantage.
Yet now, the bodies of all four mysterious experts had been reduced to fragments drifting through the universe.
This proved only one thing.
Even while suppressed, those Oracle-grade experts were not Daniel’s match.
Daniel’s combat strength was powerful enough to crush every existence of the same Rank.
He was invincible among his peers.
The experts watching from the shadows had personally witnessed the terrifying laws and Sacred Arts Daniel had unleashed during the battle.
The suppressed high-stage Oracle-grade experts had been forced to rely entirely upon the Divine-grade and Oracle-grade treasures in their possession to defend themselves.
Their own law-based Sacred Arts could not contend with Daniel’s techniques at all.
They could not even block them.
What was even more outrageous was what had happened to the Divine-grade treasures they released.
The moment Daniel summoned a basin-shaped treasure surrounded by seven-colored radiance, every one of their Divine-grade treasures lost the ability to function.
They were forcibly drawn into the seven-colored basin one after another, completely beyond their owners’ control.
In the end, the treasures were even transformed into artifacts belonging to Daniel.

sentences.text: [Nameless Omnipotent Treasure]
[Grade]: Primordial Supreme Treasure
[Type]: Auxiliary Material
[Effects]:
It can be used as a material for refining and enhancing other treasures, or as the embryo of a new treasure.
It can specifically raise the grade of any treasure.
Alternatively, the user may refine one of their own Sacred Arts into it, transforming the treasure into a personal artifact with a compatibility rate of up to 100%.
[Note]:
The exact effects depend upon the number of Nameless Omnipotent Treasures used.
The greater the quantity, the higher the grade to which the target treasure may be raised, and the greater the probability of achieving 100% compatibility.
At present, these treasures can raise a single Divine-grade treasure to Primordial Supreme Treasure-grade at most.
[Description]:
As its name suggests, the Nameless Omnipotent Treasure can be used for almost anything.
It may serve as a crafting or fusion material to raise the grade of another treasure.
It may also be used as a treasure embryo to forge a personal artifact uniquely suited to its owner.
It can even replicate one of the user’s Sacred Arts, engraving an identical ability into the artifact and transforming it into an exclusive sacred treasure.
After reading the description and effects of the Nameless Omnipotent Treasure, a golden gleam immediately appeared in Daniel’s eyes.
Its applications were far broader than those of the Vigilance Crystal he had obtained earlier.
More importantly, its enhancement limit reached peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasure level.
That was almost the same grade as the black Divine Spear in his possession.
Daniel had previously been frustrated by his inability to find a way to advance the Voidbound Grail.
Now that he possessed these Nameless Omnipotent Treasures, he finally had an opportunity to upgrade it.
If he successfully advanced the Voidbound Grail, he would possess more than five treasures at Primordial Supreme Treasure-grade or above.
With that thought, Daniel did not hesitate.
He raised his hand and retrieved the Voidbound Grail he had used earlier.
He then exerted a small amount of power and tossed several Nameless Omnipotent Treasures into it.
The two immediately began to fuse.
Like ripples of liquid, the Nameless Omnipotent Treasures smoothly merged into the Voidbound Grail.
However, the grail did not appear to change at all.
It did not even release the slightest flash of unusual light.
After thinking for a moment, Daniel guessed that he had not used enough of them.
He immediately threw all the remaining Nameless Omnipotent Treasures into the grail.
Just like the previous ones, they transformed into watery ripples and rapidly sank into the Voidbound Grail.
Sure enough, the moment the final treasures entered, a system notification rang in his ears.
[Ding!
Congratulations, Player.
The Voidbound Grail has successfully completed its advancement!]
[Current Grade of the Voidbound Grail: Primordial Supreme Treasure!]
[Ding!
This advancement has triggered the amplification effect!]
[Congratulations, Player.
You have obtained the peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasure: Voidbound Grail — Treasure Spirit Awakened!]
Several notifications rang out in succession, and a smile immediately appeared on Daniel’s face.
As expected, as long as he possessed enough Nameless Omnipotent Treasures, the Voidbound Grail could be advanced.
What surprised him even more was that the advancement had triggered an amplification effect.
It had directly raised the Voidbound Grail to peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasure level.
It had even awakened a Treasure Spirit.
Daniel immediately began carefully examining the grail in his hand, eager to see how it had changed after advancing.
The upgraded Voidbound Grail had now reached the same grade as his black Divine Spear.
After observing it for only a few moments, Daniel discovered the tremendous changes brought about by its advancement.
"As expected, the Voidbound Grail’s effects have improved by far more than a single level."
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Before its advancement, the Voidbound Grail could affect only treasures at Primordial Law-grade or below.
Now, however, its spatial sealing ability could even influence peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasures.
In other words, the current Voidbound Grail could unconditionally suppress every Divine-grade treasure at peak-grade Primordial Supreme Treasure level or below.
Furthermore, no existence beneath high-stage Oracle-grade could break through the spacetime-sealing domain created by the Voidbound Grail.
The upgraded grail had even obtained an additional characteristic—
Impervious to All Laws.
Just like Daniel’s black Divine Spear, it could now resist law-based Sacred Arts released by high-stage Oracle-grade experts.
After its advancement, the Voidbound Grail could truly be regarded as an exceptional supreme treasure.
The large number of Nameless Omnipotent Treasures Daniel had consumed had not been wasted.
After finishing his inspection of all his gains, Daniel did not linger.
He returned directly to the Emperor-class sacred vessel and continued on his journey.

chapters.title: Chapter 461 -461-Intimidating the Enemy
paragraphs: Judging from the combat power Daniel had displayed, the only way to deal with him was through Oracle-grade treasures.
However, during the previous battle, Daniel’s Oracle-grade treasures had clearly been far more powerful than theirs.
Whenever they used one of their own treasures, it was destroyed.
Under ordinary circumstances, they would not even be willing to bring them out.
Daniel, on the other hand, had casually thrown out an entire handful at once.
He possessed treasures of every possible tier—T7, T8, and perhaps even T9.
Their overwhelming power had completely crushed the ordinary Oracle-grade treasures of his opponents.
He could even forcibly seize Divine-grade treasures.
How were they supposed to fight an opponent like that?
"What should we do now?"
"What else can we do? Retreat immediately."
"You don’t seriously believe we can defeat him, do you?"
"Could that man be a half-step Eternal expert?"
"His strength is far too terrifying. Otherwise, why is he able to display such overwhelming combat power when all of us are being suppressed by the Great Dao?"
"Exactly. Not only is he immensely powerful, but his reserves of Divine-grade treasures are also far greater than ours."
"That man is practically a monster."
"Throughout the entire battle, I could not identify a single weakness."
"He seemed like an omnipotent existence who completely surpassed ordinary experts like us."
"Compared to him, the hundreds of thousands of years I spent cultivating almost feel meaningless."
"Who could disagree?"
"We should leave immediately and abandon the ambush."
"The mysterious experts serving Prince Lucian are already dead. At the very least, they helped us test Daniel’s strength."
"Now that we understand how terrifying he is, we cannot foolishly charge forward and throw away our lives."
All three of them were experts belonging to Prince Alvin’s faction.
The reason they had not acted earlier was that they had remained hidden, observing the battle and waiting for an opportunity.
If the experts from Prince Lucian’s faction successfully killed Daniel, then everything would be settled, and they could simply return to report the result.
If the four mysterious experts from Lucian’s faction managed to entangle Daniel and leave him close to death, they would not have minded emerging to deliver the final blow.
Afterward, they could even conveniently eliminate Lucian’s remaining supporters as well.
But given the current situation, killing Daniel was out of the question.
They would already be fortunate if Daniel did not come looking for them.
"Ahem."
One of the three experts suddenly cleared his throat.
"No matter what the two of you decide, I am going back."
"Only a lunatic would continue provoking a monster like that."
"I have no desire to die here so soon."
"I am already close to facing my T8 Great Dao Tribulation. I need to return and prepare properly."
As soon as he finished speaking, his figure rapidly faded from the spot.
The remaining two experts exchanged helpless glances.
Neither of them possessed the slightest confidence.
For some inexplicable reason, they felt that even if their side had ten times as many people, they still might not be Daniel’s match.
Now, only the two of them remained.
After staring at one another for a long moment, they reached the same decision.
"We should leave."
"Agreed. Returning is the wiser choice."
Prince Lucian’s faction had directly lost four powerful experts.
Meanwhile, the three experts from Prince Alvin’s faction had spent a long time lying in ambush, only to discover that they were completely outmatched.
In the end, they all fled with their tails between their legs.
Only a few experts belonging to the second-tier princes remained.
When they looked around and realized how isolated they were, they also lost all desire to continue the ambush.
"Forget it. We cannot possibly defeat that man."
"We should leave immediately."
"Exactly. I’m leaving as well."
"Challenging him alone would be no different from seeking death."
"That man is simply too powerful."
"Everyone else is already retreating, so our absence will not make any difference."
"No one can blame us after we return."
Daniel had no idea that the strength he displayed across two consecutive battles had completely terrified every remaining hostile expert.
In the first battle, Daniel killed a T7 Oracle-grade expert.
That victory caused the experts of the same faction to unite against him.
At the time, they merely believed that none of them could defeat him alone.
If they joined forces, perhaps they would have a chance.
Then came the second battle.
Daniel single-handedly suppressed four mysterious experts from Prince Lucian’s faction and annihilated every one of them on the spot.
He had practically destroyed the largest organized group supporting any prince currently present.
That display also frightened away the three great experts of Prince Alvin’s faction.
As for the factions of the second-tier princes, there was even less to say.
The bloody fate of those who had attacked Daniel had occurred only moments earlier.
Within a short time, every mysterious expert hidden throughout the surrounding region retreated.
Not a single person dared remain.
All of them disappeared without a trace.
Daniel continued traveling aboard his Emperor-class sacred vessel.
Before departing, he had already gained a clear understanding of his mission.
The Heavenly River Starfield was an enormous imperial territory.
Under its jurisdiction was the Kafu Plane, which was itself considered one of the great worlds.
Unfortunately, the Kafu World had suffered terrible luck.
It happened to lie directly at the site of a Great Dao Tribulation Cloud eruption.
There were numerous eruption points for Great Dao Tribulation Clouds throughout this universe.
Daniel had learned of this only after consulting a wide variety of ancient records.
The eruption points were densely distributed and extremely unstable.
No one knew when one would erupt.
They could appear randomly in any location.
As a result, Great Dao Tribulation Clouds often erupted without warning and completely destroyed entire planes.
This was precisely why the empire’s legions had been scattered throughout its territories.
Each legion was stationed within a relatively large plane so that it could suppress disasters whenever they appeared.
Why had the Heavenly River Starfield not requested assistance from the imperial legions the moment the Great Dao Tribulation Cloud erupted?
The nearest legion was already engaged in an intense battle against Tribulation-Ash Monsters.
It simply could not spare any manpower to support the Heavenly River Starfield.
Furthermore, whenever a tribulation cloud erupted within a single great plane, the Oracle Hall was generally unwilling to mobilize a major force to deal with it.
Therefore, the Holy See’s original intention had been to dispatch a powerful Oracle-grade squad to resolve the disaster within the Kafu Plane.
Through Daniel’s careful maneuvering, Prince Dorek’s faction successfully obtained control of the mission.
The Eternal Emperor had summoned Dorek only two days earlier.
He had been reasonably satisfied with Dorek’s performance.
Perhaps the Emperor had already begun to regard Dorek as a capable and promising talent.
In addition, Daniel’s agents within the Holy See had quietly manipulated the situation.
As a result, the mission was directly assigned to Prince Dorek as a test.
However, Dorek himself was occupied with the struggle for imperial power.
Naturally, he could not leave the Imperial City.
At this stage, the closer he remained to the center of power, the better.
If he left, an enormous disturbance might erupt in his absence and permanently destroy his chances of ascending the imperial throne.

chapters.title: Chapter 462 -462-Dealing with the Corruption
paragraphs: Prince Dorek had been granted another private audience with the Eternal Emperor at such a critical moment.
He had even been allowed to attend the imperial court assembly.
The other princes were already red-eyed with jealousy.
Some of them were practically going mad with rage.
It was precisely because of this that Daniel had been forced to consider the risks to Dorek’s safety and persuade him to hand over the mission.
This arrangement allowed Dorek to remain within the Imperial City, at the heart of imperial power, while also ensuring that the mission would be completed.
Naturally, the majority of the resulting merit would be credited to Daniel.
Of course, Dorek would still receive recognition for recommending him.
Daniel, meanwhile, could use this opportunity to obtain an official position and formally enter the Holy See.
The Holy See would probably not be stingy with its appointment.
He might receive a relatively high-ranking position from the very beginning.
That would not only grant him a fixed monthly supply of Realm-Crosser Points, but also bestow a corresponding racial talent upon humanity.
Daniel and Dorek had coordinated this entire performance with exceptional precision.
Only through such cooperation could they achieve the ideal result.
Now that Daniel had eliminated two groups of mysterious experts sent to assassinate him, his most important task was to fulfill his responsibility as Supreme Commander—
Suppress every Tribulation-Ash Monster within the Heavenly River Starfield.
Within the Uma Plane of the Heavenly River Starfield—
It was the great world closest to the Tribulation-Ash Monsters that had not yet completely fallen.
The officials responsible for governing the entire starfield had just received word that the Holy See had dispatched a Supreme Commander.
He would soon descend upon their plane and help them resolve the Tribulation-Ash disaster.
"Are they serious?"
"They didn’t send a single soldier. What use is there in sending only a Supreme Commander?"
"Exactly. They might as well have sent an Oracle-grade combat squad."
"I heard that the Supreme Commander is only Divine-grade."
"A cultivator of that Rank is completely useless against a situation that has already deteriorated this badly."
"The outbreak in the Kafu Plane is still relatively small in scale."
"The Tribulation-Ash Monsters there aren’t particularly powerful. A few T7 high-stage Oracle-grade experts should be enough to eliminate them all."
"Yet the Oracle Hall has chosen to stand by and do nothing."
"Even now, they have sent only a single Divine-grade expert. I truly don’t understand what they are thinking."
"It is probably because the struggle for the imperial throne has become too intense recently."
"The situation within the Holy See is extremely complicated. They cannot casually deploy Oracle-grade combat forces."
The moment the imperial succession struggle was mentioned, everyone immediately fell silent.
None of them dared continue discussing it.
The waters surrounding that matter were simply too deep.
"The Supreme Commander should arrive soon."
"Tch. What difference will his arrival make?"
"In the end, we’ll probably still have to take action ourselves, gather local experts, and suppress the spread of tribulation-ash corruption."
"The corruption is spreading everywhere."
"It will probably reach the Uma Plane soon."
"If that Supreme Commander travels quickly enough, perhaps he can at least arrive before our plane falls completely."
It was common knowledge that Tribulation-Ash Monsters were bizarre creatures controlled by newly born Divine Souls after powerful beings were corrupted by tribulation ash.
They could no longer be considered human.
They knew only destruction and slaughter.
Yet they retained all the strength and cultivation Ranks they had possessed while alive.
That was what made them truly terrifying.
The beings capable of surviving long enough to be transformed into Tribulation-Ash Monsters were almost always Divine-grade or above.
When countless Divine-grade experts were transformed simultaneously, the initial outbreak was often extraordinarily violent.
Only an Oracle-grade squad dispatched by the Eternal Empire could suppress them.
Large-scale Tribulation-Ash disasters frequently erupted throughout the Eternal Empire.
Some outbreaks had even produced Oracle-grade monsters.
Tribulation-Ash Monsters above T7 were no weaker than ordinary T7 Oracle-grade experts.
Only a coordinated Oracle-grade squad could suppress such existences.
Although the outbreak in the Heavenly River Starfield was considered small in scale, it still could not be underestimated.
Its strongest monster was a T7 Tribulation-Ash Monster.
There were also several T6 Tribulation-Ash Monsters.
That was already an extremely serious disaster.
Yet the Holy See had dispatched only a single Supreme Commander.
It seemed the Holy See had never seriously considered how the mission was supposed to be completed.
Once the entire Heavenly River Starfield fell, they would probably place all the blame upon Dorek.
After all, the person selected to carry out the mission belonged to his faction.
Naturally, he would be held fully responsible.
At this moment, Daniel’s Emperor-class sacred vessel had just entered the Heavenly River Starfield.
He had arrived even faster than many local experts had predicted.
"I’ve finally reached the Heavenly River Starfield."
"The Tribulation-Ash Monsters should not have reached the Uma Plane yet."
"I’ll head there first and assess the situation."
Daniel gazed upon the magnificent starry sky and quickly made his decision.
The Uma Plane occupied an extremely important position within the Heavenly River Starfield.
Through various information channels, Daniel had already learned that the starfield’s governing authorities had gathered there.
He needed to visit the plane and assume command over all local forces.
Before long, the outline of the Uma Plane appeared ahead of the sacred vessel.
Daniel did not slow down.
He piloted the ship directly into the plane and eventually docked at a nearby harbor.
Once the vessel came to a stop, he put it away and flew alone toward the official city below.
The moment he approached, a soldier guarding the city gate stopped him.
"Halt!"
"Tribulation-Ash Monsters are currently causing chaos throughout the region."
"As part of our routine inspection, open your storage space."
Daniel frowned slightly upon hearing those words.
No matter how severe the Tribulation-Ash outbreak became, there was no reason to inspect someone’s storage space.
Tribulation-Ash Monsters could not hide inside a storage artifact.
The soldier claimed that this was an official inspection, but he was most likely attempting to use the opportunity to extort several valuables from Daniel.
The Uma World was extremely far from the Eternal Empire’s central territories.
It seemed corruption had already spread from the upper levels of government all the way down to its roots.
These people relied upon their official status and showed no respect toward the remaining experts in the region.
They extorted whatever they could without caring whether Divine-grade cultivators lived or died.
A mere gate guard dared order a Divine-grade expert to expose his private storage space.
His intentions were obvious.
Daniel sneered.
"My hearing isn’t very good."
"What did you just say?"
"I didn’t hear you clearly."
The gate guard sensed the terrifying pressure emanating from Daniel.
Daniel had not yet revealed his cultivation aura, but the invisible oppression alone was enough to make the soldier feel greatly threatened.
The guard instinctively stepped backward in fear before shouting sternly,
"What do you mean by that?"
"What are you trying to do?"
"I am merely carrying out my official duties!"
The corners of Daniel’s mouth rose slightly.
"Official duties?"
"Is this how you carry them out?"
"You dare attempt to extort a bribe from me?"
"You must be tired of living."
The moment those words fell, light suddenly erupted from Daniel’s body.
The Holy Spirit Stone appeared without warning.
It instantly transformed into a streak of light and pierced straight through the gate guard’s head.
The surrounding civilians and nearby soldiers stared at the scene in stunned horror.
Someone had actually killed one of the city’s gate guards in broad daylight!

The officials responsible for governing the entire starfield had just received word that the Holy See had dispatched a Supreme Commander.
He would soon descend upon their plane and help them resolve the Tribulation-Ash disaster.
"Are they serious?"
"They didn’t send a single soldier.
What use is there in sending only a Supreme Commander?"
"Exactly.
They might as well have sent an Oracle-grade combat squad."
"I heard that the Supreme Commander is only Divine-grade."
"A cultivator of that Rank is completely useless against a situation that has already deteriorated this badly."
"The outbreak in the Kafu Plane is still relatively small in scale."
"The Tribulation-Ash Monsters there aren’t particularly powerful.
A few T7 high-stage Oracle-grade experts should be enough to eliminate them all."
"Yet the Oracle Hall has chosen to stand by and do nothing."
"Even now, they have sent only a single Divine-grade expert.
I truly don’t understand what they are thinking."
"It is probably because the struggle for the imperial throne has become too intense recently."
"The situation within the Holy See is extremely complicated.
They cannot casually deploy Oracle-grade combat forces."
The moment the imperial succession struggle was mentioned, everyone immediately fell silent.
None of them dared continue discussing it.
The waters surrounding that matter were simply too deep.
"The Supreme Commander should arrive soon."
"Tch.
What difference will his arrival make?"
"In the end, we’ll probably still have to take action ourselves, gather local experts, and suppress the spread of tribulation-ash corruption."
"The corruption is spreading everywhere."
"It will probably reach the Uma Plane soon."
"If that Supreme Commander travels quickly enough, perhaps he can at least arrive before our plane falls completely."
It was common knowledge that Tribulation-Ash Monsters were bizarre creatures controlled by newly born Divine Souls after powerful beings were corrupted by tribulation ash.
They could no longer be considered human.
They knew only destruction and slaughter.
Yet they retained all the strength and cultivation Ranks they had possessed while alive.
That was what made them truly terrifying.
The beings capable of surviving long enough to be transformed into Tribulation-Ash Monsters were almost always Divine-grade or above.
When countless Divine-grade experts were transformed simultaneously, the initial outbreak was often extraordinarily violent.
Only an Oracle-grade squad dispatched by the Eternal Empire could suppress them.
Large-scale Tribulation-Ash disasters frequently erupted throughout the Eternal Empire.
Some outbreaks had even produced Oracle-grade monsters.
Tribulation-Ash Monsters above T7 were no weaker than ordinary T7 Oracle-grade experts.
Only a coordinated Oracle-grade squad could suppress such existences.
Although the outbreak in the Heavenly River Starfield was considered small in scale, it still could not be underestimated.
Its strongest monster was a T7 Tribulation-Ash Monster.
There were also several T6 Tribulation-Ash Monsters.
That was already an extremely serious disaster.
Yet the Holy See had dispatched only a single Supreme Commander.
It seemed the Holy See had never seriously considered how the mission was supposed to be completed.
Once the entire Heavenly River Starfield fell, they would probably place all the blame upon Dorek.
After all, the person selected to carry out the mission belonged to his faction.
Naturally, he would be held fully responsible.
At this moment, Daniel’s Emperor-class sacred vessel had just entered the Heavenly River Starfield.
He had arrived even faster than many local experts had predicted.
"I’ve finally reached the Heavenly River Starfield."
"The Tribulation-Ash Monsters should not have reached the Uma Plane yet."
"I’ll head there first and assess the situation."
Daniel gazed upon the magnificent starry sky and quickly made his decision.
The Uma Plane occupied an extremely important position within the Heavenly River Starfield.
Through various information channels, Daniel had already learned that the starfield’s governing authorities had gathered there.
He needed to visit the plane and assume command over all local forces.
Before long, the outline of the Uma Plane appeared ahead of the sacred vessel.
Daniel did not slow down.
He piloted the ship directly into the plane and eventually docked at a nearby harbor.
Once the vessel came to a stop, he put it away and flew alone toward the official city below.
The moment he approached, a soldier guarding the city gate stopped him.
"Halt!"
"Tribulation-Ash Monsters are currently causing chaos throughout the region."
"As part of our routine inspection, open your storage space."
Daniel frowned slightly upon hearing those words.
No matter how severe the Tribulation-Ash outbreak became, there was no reason to inspect someone’s storage space.
Tribulation-Ash Monsters could not hide inside a storage artifact.
The soldier claimed that this was an official inspection, but he was most likely attempting to use the opportunity to extort several valuables from Daniel.
The Uma World was extremely far from the Eternal Empire’s central territories.
It seemed corruption had already spread from the upper levels of government all the way down to its roots.
These people relied upon their official status and showed no respect toward the remaining experts in the region.
They extorted whatever they could without caring whether Divine-grade cultivators lived or died.
A mere gate guard dared order a Divine-grade expert to expose his private storage space.
His intentions were obvious.
Daniel sneered.
"My hearing isn’t very good."
"What did you just say?"
"I didn’t hear you clearly."
The gate guard sensed the terrifying pressure emanating from Daniel.
Daniel had not yet revealed his cultivation aura, but the invisible oppression alone was enough to make the soldier feel greatly threatened.
The guard instinctively stepped backward in fear before shouting sternly,
"What do you mean by that?"
"What are you trying to do?"
"I am merely carrying out my official duties!"
The corners of Daniel’s mouth rose slightly.
"Official duties?"
"Is this how you carry them out?"
"You dare attempt to extort a bribe from me?"
"You must be tired of living."
The moment those words fell, light suddenly erupted from Daniel’s body.
The Holy Spirit Stone appeared without warning.
It instantly transformed into a streak of light and pierced straight through the gate guard’s head.
The surrounding civilians and nearby soldiers stared at the scene in stunned horror.
Someone had actually killed one of the city’s gate guards in broad daylight!

chapters.title: Chapter 463 -463-Severe Tribulation-Ash Corruption
paragraphs: "Someone is rebelling!"
The next moment, a piercing alarm rang out.
The other gate guards immediately sounded their warning horns, and a group of soldiers who had not even reached Divine-grade rushed over, surrounding Daniel from every direction.
However, none of them dared approach.
Their faces were filled with fear and nervousness, and their postures were more timid than the last.
Daniel sneered inwardly when he saw their pathetic appearance.
What a worthless group of scum.
Before long, several officials within the city heard the commotion and hurried over.
Surprisingly, every one of them was a Divine-grade expert.
One of them stepped forward and looked Daniel up and down.
"Do you understand your crime?"
"I advise you to surrender immediately. Otherwise, the Holy See will issue a universal warrant for your arrest."
Daniel did not even bother looking at him.
He merely asked indifferently,
"What crime have I committed?"
The expert snorted coldly.
"The corpse on the ground is proof of your crime."
"You dared kill one of our city guards. Such an act is equivalent to rebellion, yet you still have the nerve to ask what crime you committed?"
"Men, seize him!"
Daniel remained completely unhurried.
He calmly took out a token from his waist.
"I will stand right here."
"Let me see who dares lay a hand on me."
"I am the Supreme Commander personally dispatched by the Holy See, entrusted with full authority to resolve the Tribulation-Ash disaster throughout the Heavenly River Starfield."
The moment they saw the token, the expressions of both the Divine-grade officials and the surrounding gate guards changed drastically.
None of them had imagined that the seemingly unremarkable young man before them was actually the Supreme Commander sent personally by the Holy See.
The surrounding area instantly fell silent.
No one even dared breathe too loudly.
Daniel coldly surveyed the experts who had been stunned senseless by his token.
"I have only just arrived, yet your people have already surrounded me."
"The man I killed attempted to extort a bribe from a Supreme Commander of the Holy See."
"Tell me—what punishment does such a crime deserve?"
The official swallowed hard.
He did not dare say a single word.
Daniel answered his own question.
"Death."
"Anyone who believes that judgment is unreasonable may step forward and debate it with me."
The group that had been acting so aggressively moments earlier immediately fell silent.
He was the Supreme Commander.
Whatever he said was the law.

Although Daniel did not yet possess a permanent official position and was only nominally the Supreme Commander assigned by the Holy See to suppress the Tribulation-Ash disaster, once he arrived here, he possessed full authority to handle all matters relating to the crisis.
He could exercise that authority at any time and in any place.
Of course, even as Supreme Commander, he could not arbitrarily place himself above every branch of the local government.
The sole responsibility of the local authorities was to fully cooperate with him in eliminating the Tribulation-Ash Monsters.
The Divine-grade official was deeply displeased.
However, there was no reason to completely fall out with a Supreme Commander of the Holy See over a mere gate guard.
Doing so would bring him no benefit whatsoever.
He could only suppress his anger and reply in a muffled voice,
"You are correct, Supreme Commander."
He waved his hand.
The guards surrounding Daniel immediately withdrew and put away their weapons, each of them still shaken by lingering fear.
The Supreme Commander before them had casually killed one of their companions with a single strike.
Had they not been bound by their duties, they would have fled the moment the attack occurred.
Since the situation had not escalated any further, that was already the best possible outcome.
Daniel rolled his neck and suddenly said,
"Bring Oracle Loka here to see me."
Oracle Loka was the local T7 powerhouse and the governor specifically assigned to defend the Heavenly River Starfield.
At present, he was also stationed within the Uma Plane.
As Supreme Commander, Daniel naturally needed to meet him.
One was the commander dispatched by the Holy See.
The other was the governor responsible for defending the region.
Only after the two sides established a working understanding could they efficiently deal with the Tribulation-Ash Monsters.
However, Daniel’s forceful attitude had greatly displeased the local officials.
It felt as though he had already replaced them and become their immediate superior.
"Oracle Loka is a high-stage Oracle-grade expert. Does a mere Divine-grade Supreme Commander truly think he can summon him whenever he pleases?"
"It is reasonable for the governor to answer the Supreme Commander’s summons, but his tone was clearly deliberate and disrespectful."
"That man from the Holy See is going to be difficult to deal with."
Many officials were dissatisfied by Daniel’s overbearing manner.
The Divine-grade expert suppressed his impatience and led Daniel into the city.
"Please follow me, Supreme Commander."
"I will take you to Oracle Loka immediately."
He then gestured for the others to remove the corpse from the ground.
As for how the matter would be handled, there was little to say.
The dead guard had simply been extraordinarily unlucky.
Of all the people he could have attempted to extort, he had chosen a Supreme Commander.
Daniel followed the official into the city and soon arrived at the government hall.
The moment he entered, he saw Oracle Loka waiting inside.
Clearly, the Oracle-grade expert had already witnessed everything that had happened outside the city.
However, he did not appear to care.
Instead, he welcomed Daniel with a broad smile.
"Welcome, honored guest who has traveled from afar."
"We are grateful that the Holy See has sent you to help resolve the troubles facing our region."
After a brief exchange of pleasantries, all the senior officials stationed there gathered together.
Daniel could already sense an extremely dense aura of corruption filling the hall.
The corruption seemed to originate from the very foundations of the city.
In reality, however, it was the scent of the Great Dao itself being corroded.
It was tribulation ash.
Daniel’s gaze sharpened slightly.
Every person present carried traces of tribulation ash upon their body.
Even the entire city had been contaminated by it.
Oracle Loka possessed the strongest aura of tribulation ash among them.
Daniel had known that this region was close to the source of the Great Dao calamity.
However, he had not expected the corruption to have become this severe.
The stronger an existence was, the faster the Great Dao Tribulation Abyss would corrupt them with tribulation ash.
The Eternal Emperor had already reached the point where he was close to being completely corrupted.
Unless he successfully survived the Eternal Tribulation, he would soon degenerate into a Tribulation-Ash Monster.
Many officials within the Holy See’s imperial court were likewise only a step away from complete corruption.
The same situation could now be seen throughout the Uma Plane.
Because it was located near the Great Dao Tribulation Abyss, the entire plane had been affected by tribulation-ash corruption.
The local governor standing before Daniel—T7 Oracle-grade Loka—was the most severely affected of them all.
The progress of Loka’s corruption was already comparable to that of the officials Daniel had seen during the Holy See’s court assembly.
Fortunately, Daniel did not say anything.
He merely frowned slightly.
He had come here only to complete his mission.
As for the problems surrounding the Great Dao Tribulation Source, someone else would naturally deal with them in the future.
With that thought, Daniel immediately moved on to the main issue.
"I intend to establish a force here capable of suppressing the Tribulation-Ash Monsters."
"Does Oracle Loka have any objections?"
Loka frowned briefly before replying indifferently,
"Since you are the Supreme Commander, the matter is naturally yours to handle."
"We need only cooperate with your orders."

chapters.title: Chapter 464 -464-Confronting the Officials
paragraphs: After hearing Oracle Loka’s answer, Daniel slowly swept his gaze across the officials gathered below the dais.
Not one of them met his eyes.

Some stared at the ceiling, while others studied the floor or turned toward the pillars as though the carvings had suddenly become fascinating. Their silence made their attitude obvious. They had no intention of cooperating with the newly arrived Supreme Commander.
Daniel frowned slightly. Then he turned back to Loka.
"In that case, Governor Loka, why don’t you serve as my deputy?"
The instant those words left his mouth, every official in the hall snapped their attention back toward him.
Several cautiously glanced at Loka, unease and alarm flashing through their eyes. They seemed to fear that the T7 Oracle-grade governor might erupt in fury at any moment.

Loka was no ordinary official. He was a genuine high-stage Oracle-grade powerhouse and the long-standing governor of the Heavenly River Starfield. Daniel, by contrast, appeared to be only Divine-grade. His temporary title of Supreme Commander might grant him authority over the Tribulation-Ash campaign, but in the eyes of the local establishment, that did not erase the enormous difference in cultivation or seniority.

If Daniel wanted Loka as his deputy, he should at least have approached him privately, negotiated the arrangement, and allowed the governor to preserve his dignity. Instead, he had issued the request in front of everyone. Accepting would make Loka appear subordinate to a young Divine-grade outsider. Refusing would openly challenge the authority of the Holy See.
Loka’s expression did not change, but his eyes narrowed.

"Supreme Commander, your will naturally takes precedence," he said evenly. "Unfortunately, I have urgent matters to attend to and cannot remain here any longer. I will take my leave. Please handle the remaining arrangements as you see fit."
With that, he rose and prepared to depart.
A cold smile appeared on Daniel’s face.
"Oracle Loka, wait. There is still one matter that has not been settled."
Loka stopped and looked back over his shoulder.
"What matter?"
Daniel did not answer.
Whoosh!
Without warning, the Holy Spirit Stone appeared before him. It transformed into a streak of golden light and crossed the hall faster than anyone below Oracle-grade could follow.
A dull impact sounded.

The stone pierced straight through the head of a quasi-Oracle-grade official standing among the local authorities. Golden light flashed once more, and the Holy Spirit Stone returned to Daniel’s side as quietly as though nothing had happened.
The armored official remained upright for a fraction of a second. Then his body collapsed heavily onto the polished floor.
He was the Chief Inspector responsible for the defense of Uma Plane’s main city.
Daniel had killed him openly, in front of Governor Loka and every senior official present.

For several breaths, the hall was completely silent. The officials stared at the corpse in disbelief. They could not understand why the Supreme Commander, who had only just arrived and was meeting them for the first time, had suddenly executed the Chief Inspector.
Even more shocking was the method. Daniel had supposedly possessed only Divine-grade cultivation, yet he had instantly killed a quasi-Oracle-grade expert before anyone could intervene.
"You!"
Loka’s expression finally changed. Rage surged across his face.

"Supreme Commander Daniel, what is the meaning of this? You killed my subordinate in front of me. If you cannot provide a satisfactory explanation, I am afraid you will not be leaving this hall today."
His aura began to stir.

"Do not think your temporary appointment places you above imperial law. Even if the Eternal Emperor himself came here, he could not casually execute an imperial official without cause. You may be Prince Dorek’s most trusted minister and perhaps a future pillar of the crown, but unless you explain yourself, this matter will not end here."
Daniel remained perfectly calm. Instead of responding at once, he studied the officials below, observing every change in their expressions.
With Loka supporting them, they quickly recovered their courage.
"The governor is correct," one official declared. "You may be the Supreme Commander, but the officials of Uma Plane deserve an explanation."
Another stepped forward.

"This region may be far from the Imperial City, but that does not mean you may kill whomever you please. If officials can be executed without charge or trial, how do you expect anyone here to obey you?"
A third spoke even more sharply.

"Perhaps the Supreme Commander believes the lives of people in remote territories are worth no more than weeds. Perhaps you think we are insects to be crushed whenever the mood strikes you. If so, what law remains in this starfield?"
Daniel allowed them to vent until their voices gradually faded. Then he spoke in an unhurried tone.
"This is indeed my first visit to Uma Plane. Yet the moment I entered the city, a gate guard stopped me. Do any of you know what he demanded?"
No one answered.
"He ordered me to open my private storage space, claiming it was part of a routine inspection."
Daniel’s voice remained level, but the atmosphere in the hall changed.
"Tell me, when did the Eternal Empire enact a law requiring every traveler to expose the contents of their storage artifacts? Was that decree issued personally by Governor Loka?"
Several officials stiffened.
Daniel turned his gaze toward Loka.

"Of course, I am certain Governor Loka knew nothing about it. Such an absurd and harmful regulation could only have been invented by corrupt subordinates who abused the governor’s authority for personal gain. Wouldn’t you agree, Oracle Loka?"
Loka’s face darkened. He said nothing.
Daniel continued as though he had only just remembered another detail.

"Ah, there is one more thing. I happen to carry a treasure capable of recording images and sound. Everything the gate guard said and did has been preserved. If anyone doubts my account, I can display the recording here and now."
His gaze swept over the assembled officials once again.

The courage they had displayed moments earlier vanished. One after another, they lowered their heads. Everyone knew how common extortion had become in remote imperial territories. More importantly, no one knew whether Daniel truly possessed such a recording treasure. Challenging him meant gambling their careers and lives on the innocence of a dead gate guard.
Daniel gave a quiet, contemptuous laugh.
"If Governor Loka believes my judgment was unjust, he may accompany me to the Holy See and contest the matter before the central authorities. I have nothing to fear from an official investigation."
He looked around the hall.
"Is anyone else willing to travel with us and testify that I acted improperly?"
Silence answered him.
Loka’s expression shifted repeatedly. Daniel had placed an enormous political burden upon him while leaving a narrow path of retreat.

If Loka rejected Daniel’s account, he would effectively admit that the corrupt inspection policy had been authorized by his own office. He could demand evidence, of course, and insist that Daniel produce the recording. Yet doing so would be dangerous. Uma Plane lay far from the Imperial City, and corruption had become so widespread that the truth hardly required investigation.

The dead Chief Inspector had overseen the city defenses. If the gate guards had been systematically extorting travelers, responsibility would naturally rise through the chain of command. The Chief Inspector was the perfect scapegoat, and Daniel had already made certain that the man could never defend himself.
Loka now understood the purpose of the sudden execution.

Daniel had not killed at random. He had chosen the one official whose death could simultaneously intimidate the local government, sever a corrupt chain of evidence, and force Loka to publicly distance himself from his own subordinate.
The officials in the hall also began to understand.
The young Supreme Commander was not merely strong. He had arrived prepared to seize control of the entire situation, and he had done so with one strike.

If officials can be executed without charge or trial, how do you expect anyone here to obey you?"
A third spoke even more sharply.
"Perhaps the Supreme Commander believes the lives of people in remote territories are worth no more than weeds.
Perhaps you think we are insects to be crushed whenever the mood strikes you.
If so, what law remains in this starfield?"
Daniel allowed them to vent until their voices gradually faded.
Then he spoke in an unhurried tone.
"This is indeed my first visit to Uma Plane.
Yet the moment I entered the city, a gate guard stopped me.
Do any of you know what he demanded?"
No one answered.
"He ordered me to open my private storage space, claiming it was part of a routine inspection."
Daniel’s voice remained level, but the atmosphere in the hall changed.
"Tell me, when did the Eternal Empire enact a law requiring every traveler to expose the contents of their storage artifacts?
Was that decree issued personally by Governor Loka?"
Several officials stiffened.
Daniel turned his gaze toward Loka.
"Of course, I am certain Governor Loka knew nothing about it.
Such an absurd and harmful regulation could only have been invented by corrupt subordinates who abused the governor’s authority for personal gain.
Wouldn’t you agree, Oracle Loka?"
Loka’s face darkened.
He said nothing.
Daniel continued as though he had only just remembered another detail.
"Ah, there is one more thing.
I happen to carry a treasure capable of recording images and sound.
Everything the gate guard said and did has been preserved.
If anyone doubts my account, I can display the recording here and now."
His gaze swept over the assembled officials once again.
The courage they had displayed moments earlier vanished.
One after another, they lowered their heads.
Everyone knew how common extortion had become in remote imperial territories.
More importantly, no one knew whether Daniel truly possessed such a recording treasure.
Challenging him meant gambling their careers and lives on the innocence of a dead gate guard.
Daniel gave a quiet, contemptuous laugh.
"If Governor Loka believes my judgment was unjust, he may accompany me to the Holy See and contest the matter before the central authorities.
I have nothing to fear from an official investigation."
He looked around the hall.
"Is anyone else willing to travel with us and testify that I acted improperly?"
Silence answered him.
Loka’s expression shifted repeatedly.
Daniel had placed an enormous political burden upon him while leaving a narrow path of retreat.
If Loka rejected Daniel’s account, he would effectively admit that the corrupt inspection policy had been authorized by his own office.
He could demand evidence, of course, and insist that Daniel produce the recording.
Yet doing so would be dangerous.
Uma Plane lay far from the Imperial City, and corruption had become so widespread that the truth hardly required investigation.
The dead Chief Inspector had overseen the city defenses.
If the gate guards had been systematically extorting travelers, responsibility would naturally rise through the chain of command.
The Chief Inspector was the perfect scapegoat, and Daniel had already made certain that the man could never defend himself.
Loka now understood the purpose of the sudden execution.
Daniel had not killed at random.

He had chosen the one official whose death could simultaneously intimidate the local government, sever a corrupt chain of evidence, and force Loka to publicly distance himself from his own subordinate.
The officials in the hall also began to understand.
The young Supreme Commander was not merely strong.
He had arrived prepared to seize control of the entire situation, and he had done so with one strike.

chapters.title: Chapter 465 -465-The Land of the Great Dao Tribulation Source
paragraphs: If the dispute were genuinely investigated, Loka knew he would gain nothing.

Daniel had already killed the Chief Inspector, the one official most likely to know the full truth behind the gate guards’ extortion. The dead could not speak, defend themselves, or shift responsibility onto anyone else. Every crime could now be placed upon the corpse.

Even if the Chief Inspector had still been alive, Loka would have needed to sacrifice him in order to protect the governor’s office. The man had become politically disposable the moment Daniel exposed the illegal inspections.
After several moments of silence, Loka slowly exhaled.

"As expected of a Supreme Commander sent by the Holy See," he said. "You uncovered the truth immediately upon your arrival. I misunderstood you earlier. As the governor of this region, I also bear a degree of responsibility for failing to discover the corruption beneath me. Thank you for cleansing my administration of a traitor."
The words sounded gracious, but everyone could hear the strain beneath them.

Loka could no longer condemn Daniel for killing his subordinate. He was now forced to thank him publicly. Whatever curses he might be hurling inside his heart were irrelevant. Before the officials of Uma Plane, Daniel had achieved an absolute victory.
The other officials changed their expressions just as quickly.

"The Supreme Commander is truly discerning," one declared. "That man had long been exploiting the people and abusing the governor’s name. Fortunately, Your Excellency saw through him and proved Governor Loka’s innocence."

"What a magnificent strike!" another added. "The traitor deserved death. To die by the Supreme Commander’s hand was almost too fortunate for him. Had he remained alive, we would have personally torn him apart for disgracing the government."
"Your Excellency eliminated a great danger the moment you arrived. Your judgment is truly admirable."
Only minutes earlier, these same people had accused Daniel of murder and tyranny. Now they competed to praise him, completely forgetting their previous outrage.

At last, they understood that the new Supreme Commander possessed far more than a temporary title. His cultivation might appear low, but his methods, courage, treasures, and political instincts were all terrifying. He had killed one man to warn a hundred and demonstrated exactly what it meant for a new official to arrive with fire in his hands.
Even Loka, a T7 Oracle-grade governor, had been forced into Daniel’s rhythm. The officials could only conclude that no one sent from the Holy See was simple.
Their contempt transformed into a mixture of fear and reluctant respect.

Once Daniel confirmed that no one would openly challenge his authority in Uma Plane, he waved his hand and dismissed the meeting. He then summoned his Emperor-class sacred vessel and prepared to inspect the Land of the Great Dao Tribulation Source.
He took none of the local officials with him.

They would be of little use in battle. Worse, escorting them would force Daniel to divide his attention between protecting unreliable subordinates and dealing with the Tribulation-Ash Monsters. He preferred to investigate alone. If fighting became necessary, he could act without restraint.
The officials watched the enormous vessel rise into the sky and disappear beyond the plane’s boundary. Only then did many of them release the breaths they had been holding.
"The Supreme Commander is personally inspecting the planes destroyed by tribulation-ash corruption," one official said. "At least he appears willing to perform real work."
Another sneered.
"What difference will that make? His strength is limited. There is no possibility that he can suppress the Tribulation-Ash Army alone."
"Exactly. If he possessed T8 Oracle-grade strength, perhaps he could eliminate the monsters without assistance. But he is merely Divine-grade."
"Just wait. He will return soon enough and beg Governor Loka to cooperate."
"After the way he humiliated the governor, even if he lowers his head and pleads for help, why should the governor truly support him?"
"The fact that the governor has not already placed obstacles in his path is an act of mercy."

None of them believed Daniel could accomplish anything alone. The Tribulation-Ash Army contained multiple T6 and T7 Oracle-grade combatants. How could a single Divine-grade commander possibly suppress them all?
Daniel, however, had no interest in their doubts.

He wanted to complete the mission as quickly as possible, return with undeniable merit, and strengthen Prince Dorek’s position in the succession struggle. The opinions of local officials were meaningless compared with that objective.
The Emperor-class sacred vessel tore through space toward the Land of the Great Dao Tribulation Source.
Before long, Daniel reached the first group of ruined planes.
The sight before him caused even his expression to change.

An entire Plane of Life had been reduced to tribulation ash. Gray-white particles drifted through the atmosphere like endless snow. Trees, mountains, rivers, lakes, oceans, and even the earth itself had lost their original forms. Everything had decayed into layers of silent ash.
No buildings remained. No roads, cities, monuments, or traces of civilization could be seen. The tribulation ash had buried history itself.
The whole plane had become a dead gray wasteland.

This was the true horror of Tribulation-Ash Monsters. The Great Dao Tribulation Source within them did not merely corrupt living creatures. It interfered with the laws governing the world, causing matter, energy, and even spiritual structures to rot into ash.
A nauseating aura of decay rushed toward Daniel. It was not the smell of ordinary death. It was the scent of laws collapsing, of a universe losing the principles that allowed life and order to exist.
Daniel silently observed the ruined world.

Perhaps this was what every universe looked like when it reached its final moment. Starfields might die and later be reborn through the cycles of the Astral Realms, but when an entire universe reached the end of its lifespan, perhaps nothing remained except this cold, drifting ash.
He continued onward.

Plane after plane passed beneath the sacred vessel. Some had been completely erased. Others retained broken fragments of land or isolated pockets of life, but every surviving region was being consumed.
Eventually, Daniel reached the great world where the main body of the Tribulation-Ash Army had gathered.
He descended into the plane and immediately realized that he was too late to save it.

The native inhabitants were still resisting, but their defenses were collapsing everywhere. The Tribulation-Ash Army advanced with unstoppable momentum, slaughtering the living and converting the dead into new monsters. Oracle-grade Tribulation-Ash Monsters moved openly across the battlefield, corrupting the plane’s sages one after another.
From high above the world, Daniel could clearly see the enemy.

Every monster had gray, lifeless skin and blood-red eyes. Their faces and bodies still resembled the people they had once been. They retained the laws, Sacred Arts, and cultivation Ranks of their former lives, but all reason and identity had vanished.

Their Divine-grade treasures were gone. Tribulation-ash corruption had consumed every artifact they carried, reducing those treasures to useless residue. Even if a Tribulation-Ash Monster somehow obtained a new Divine-grade treasure, the artifact would soon be corroded and rendered unusable.
That weakness offered Daniel a small advantage, but it did not make the army harmless.
A warrior stripped of weapons was still terrifying when that warrior possessed Oracle-grade power and cared nothing for survival.
Below him, another city vanished beneath the gray tide.
Daniel’s gaze turned cold.
The local officials had expected him to return and beg for assistance.
Instead, he intended to end the disaster before they even understood that the battle had begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 466 -466-Suppressing the Tribulation Ash
paragraphs: Countless gray-skinned Tribulation-Ash Monsters crowded together until they formed a tide stretching beyond the horizon.

From Daniel’s position high above the plane, the army resembled an endless sea of ash. Wherever it passed, nothing living remained. Forests collapsed into powder. Rivers turned gray and still. Cities disappeared beneath waves of corrupted bodies.
Only one corner of the world still contained life.

The last surviving inhabitants had gathered behind layered formations, burning their remaining Origin and treasures to preserve a small island of green. Their defenses endured for less than two seconds after Daniel arrived.
The Tribulation-Ash tide struck.
The formations shattered. The final sanctuary vanished beneath the gray wave before Daniel could intervene.

Those killed by the monsters did not remain dead for long. Tribulation ash invaded their corpses, rewrote their Divine Souls, and raised them as new members of the army. Memories, affection, and reason disappeared. The newly transformed monsters immediately attacked the companions and relatives they had defended moments earlier.

The scene resembled an undead catastrophe, but these creatures were far more dangerous than common undead. They retained nearly all of their original cultivation and combat experience. Daniel had barely entered the plane before the entire world fell.
Even he drew in a cold breath at the speed of the conquest.

More disturbing than the slaughter was the complete destruction of life itself. Wherever the Tribulation-Ash Monsters traveled, the last traces of green vanished. If such an army spread across the entire universe, every plane and starfield would eventually become silent.
And this was considered only a small outbreak.

The strongest creature here was merely T7 Oracle-grade. The imperial legions stationed elsewhere were confronting large-scale Tribulation-Ash disasters containing T9 Oracle-grade monsters. Those stronger creatures were not mindless, either. The greater their Rank, the more intelligence they retained. At sufficiently high levels, a Tribulation-Ash Monster could possess wisdom equal to or even greater than what it had held in life.
Daniel calmly took out his Divine-grade treasures.
The time for observation had ended.

The main force of the Tribulation-Ash Army was still concentrated inside this plane. That made the world a perfect cage. Rather than allow the monsters to scatter across the Heavenly River Starfield, Daniel would seal the entire plane and destroy them here.
"Voidbound Grail."
Golden light gathered above his palm.

The upgraded Voidbound Grail appeared and began to tremble. Laws rotated around its body in countless interlocking circles. A low hum spread through the sky as invisible spatial fluctuations expanded in every direction.
Within moments, the grail’s sealing field covered the entire great world.
The boundaries of the plane solidified. Space became dense and unyielding. Every path leading outward was closed.
Then Daniel raised his other hand.
The black Divine Spear emerged.

Its shaft expanded at a terrifying speed. In only a few seconds, the spear stretched across hundreds of millions of kilometers until it appeared almost as vast as the plane itself. Its shadow fell over continents, seas, and the endless gray army below.
"Clones, manifest."

Nine figures separated from Daniel and took their positions throughout the sky. Above every clone appeared a vast projection of the Banner of Destiny’s Judgment. At the same time, phantoms of the Human Forefather emerged one after another, each carrying Oracle-grade pressure.
The laws flooding the plane began to tremble.
That disturbance immediately attracted the attention of the Oracle-grade combatants hidden within the Tribulation-Ash tide.
Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!
Gray figures appeared around Daniel in rapid succession.
There were hundreds of them.
Scarlet eyes locked onto him. Law-based Sacred Arts formed around their bodies, filling the sky with a terrifying aura of destruction.
Daniel did not retreat.
He looked at them coldly and lowered his hand.
The black Divine Spear descended.
Rumble!

A boundless spear force erupted across the world. Entire regions of the Tribulation-Ash Army vanished instantly. Monsters by the millions were ground into dust before they could even raise their heads.
That first strike was only the beginning.
The Divine Spear thrust again.
Then a third time.

Wave after wave of spear force swept across the plane. The advancing Oracle-grade monsters were forced back, and the Sacred Arts they released were crushed within the black storm. Without the protection of their strongest combatants, the ordinary Tribulation-Ash Monsters below disappeared in enormous sections.
The Oracle-grade creatures roared in fury.

They abandoned all thought of defense and charged directly toward Daniel. They had been born from the desire to destroy everything, and that impulse included their own existence. They did not care whether they survived as long as they could drag Daniel into ruin.
Their suicidal assault gave Daniel a slight headache.

The monsters represented almost every Oracle-grade tier. Some were first-stage Oracle-grade. Others had reached T6. Several emitted the pressure of T7 powerhouses. More than a hundred attacked simultaneously.
Daniel sighed.
A shield appeared before him.

The moment it manifested, countless Oracle-grade Sacred Arts crashed against its surface. Light and law exploded across the sky, but the shield did not move. As a T7 Oracle-grade treasure, it could perfectly withstand attacks from experts of the same tier.
At the same time, a collection of new Oracle-grade treasures appeared around Daniel.
"Kill."
At his command, the treasures shot forward.
Some transformed into enormous blades. Others became mountains, stars, chains, or beasts made of law. Several were genuine T7 Oracle-grade treasures. Their combined pressure shook the sealed plane.
The Tribulation-Ash Monsters had no artifacts of their own with which to resist.
The first wave of treasures tore through them.
Hundreds of Oracle-grade monsters were killed almost instantly. Their bodies disintegrated into gray fragments, and the sea of ordinary monsters beneath them collapsed under the remaining force.
Yet no system notifications sounded in Daniel’s ears.

There were no experience rewards, no treasures, and no Origin Crystals. The Tribulation-Ash Monsters appeared to exist outside the system’s ordinary rules. Daniel could destroy them, but their deaths brought him nothing.
He did not care.
This battle was being fought for official merit, Realm-Crosser Points, and Dorek’s political future. Those rewards were far more valuable than ordinary loot.
After eliminating every Oracle-grade monster except the remaining T7 leaders, Daniel raised his hand once more.
A T8 Oracle-grade treasure appeared in his palm.
"Once these last T7 creatures are gone, the mission will be complete."
He released the treasure.

In the next instant, it transformed into an enormous sacred mountain. Its shadow covered the last surviving T7 Tribulation-Ash Monsters. Before they could scatter, the mountain descended and suppressed them completely.
The world shook.
When the dust settled, the main Tribulation-Ash Army was gone.
One man had exterminated an army that had destroyed multiple planes.
Only a gray-white world remained, stripped of life and covered in tribulation ash.

Daniel had achieved this result through the overwhelming foundations he had accumulated. Treasures that would have represented the ultimate resources of entire factions were disposable weapons in his hands.

The army destroyed here accounted for roughly ninety percent of the entire outbreak. Smaller groups of monsters still wandered through medium and minor planes, but those remnants no longer posed a strategic threat. A single local Oracle-grade force could eliminate them.
Daniel decided not to visit those smaller battlefields.

He would leave the remaining merit to the officials of Uma Plane. Doing so gave them enough credit to preserve their dignity while ensuring that Daniel’s own contribution remained overwhelming and impossible to dispute.
With the main objective completed, he recalled his clones, treasures, and the Voidbound Grail. The Emperor-class sacred vessel reappeared beneath him.
Daniel set a course back to Uma Plane.
By the time the local officials received word that his vessel had returned, none of them had the slightest idea that the disaster they feared had already been brought to an end.
