chapters.title: Chapter 467 -467-A Flawless Record
paragraphs: When the officials of Uma Plane first learned that Daniel’s Emperor-class sacred vessel had returned, they assumed he had merely completed his reconnaissance.

In their minds, the next step was obvious. The Supreme Commander would gather the local authorities, explain what he had discovered, and begin arranging defensive formations and troop deployments. Not one of them imagined that Daniel had already annihilated the main body of the Tribulation-Ash Army by himself.
Sure enough, when Daniel summoned the senior officials, most arrived carrying maps, military reports, and prepared suggestions for the coming campaign. Governor Loka also appeared.
The moment he entered the hall, Loka spoke in a faintly mocking tone.

"Supreme Commander, you have spent most of your time within the Holy See. I imagine you have had few opportunities to face Tribulation-Ash Monsters directly. During your reconnaissance, were you able to confirm the location and scale of their main force?"
Daniel smiled calmly.
"Naturally. I found them."
The officials showed no surprise. They exchanged weary looks and began sighing among themselves.
"The Heavenly River Legion is currently suppressing a much larger Tribulation-Ash disaster elsewhere in the starfield," one said. "We cannot expect meaningful reinforcements in the near future."
"If the legion had been free, this outbreak would have been eliminated long ago," another replied. "Unfortunately, we can only rely on the forces already here."
A third official unfolded a map.

"We should reignite the defensive beacons and prepare the ancient formations. The Tribulation-Ash Army will eventually reach Uma Plane. Our priority should be preserving the population and holding the main cities."
Loka nodded with grave authority.
"Supreme Commander, this matter must be treated with the utmost caution. I strongly recommend that we avoid taking the initiative. A defensive strategy is far more suitable."
His statement immediately received widespread support.
"Governor Loka is correct. We must defend rather than attack."
"The enemy is too powerful for our current forces. Leaving the plane would be equivalent to offering our lives for nothing."
"We should strengthen the barriers first and wait for an opportunity."

Daniel listened without interrupting. Their arguments continued for several minutes, growing increasingly detailed. Some discussed supply routes. Others proposed abandoning the outer cities and concentrating everyone in the central region. A few spoke as though a prolonged siege were already inevitable.
Only after everyone had finished did Daniel speak.
"There is something I should tell you. The main force of the Tribulation-Ash Army has already been destroyed."
The hall went silent.
Every official stared at him. Even Loka looked genuinely confused.
After a long pause, the governor finally asked, "Supreme Commander, what did you just say? I may not have heard you clearly."
The others leaned forward, afraid of missing a single word. They were certain they had misunderstood him.
Daniel’s faint smile remained unchanged.
"I said that I have already eliminated the main Tribulation-Ash Army."
Sharp breaths sounded throughout the hall.
Impossible.

That army had erased multiple planes and contained numerous Oracle-grade monsters. Daniel had been gone for only a short time. Much of that time should have been consumed by travel alone. Was he claiming that in the remaining interval he had casually destroyed a force capable of threatening the entire Heavenly River Starfield?
Loka’s disbelief was obvious.
"The Supreme Commander is certainly an exceptional talent," he said carefully. "However, this matter concerns the lives of everyone in the region. It would be inappropriate to joke about it."
Daniel looked at him coldly.
"When have I ever joked with you?"
Loka’s eyes widened. His breathing quickened despite himself.
"You truly destroyed their main force?"
Questions erupted from below.
"Supreme Commander, the army contained high-stage Oracle-grade monsters and countless powerful sages. How could you possibly deal with all of them alone?"
"Even if you had the power to win, the battle should have lasted days. Why did you return so quickly?"
"Are you certain the monsters were not merely hiding or relocating?"
Daniel swept his gaze across the doubting officials.
"Anyone who does not believe me may investigate personally. Just remember your words when the truth strikes you in the face."
The officials immediately turned toward Loka. Despite Daniel’s formal command, Loka remained the figure they had followed for years. They waited for his decision.
The governor’s gaze flickered. Finally, he gritted his teeth.
"Since the Supreme Commander is so certain, I will send someone to verify the situation. The safety of the empire is involved. We must establish the facts beyond doubt."
He selected a fast-moving Oracle-grade scout and dispatched him at once.

The hall remained tense while they waited. Some officials whispered that Daniel must have exaggerated. Others began considering the frightening possibility that he had spoken the truth. Loka sat in silence, his expression growing more severe with every passing moment.
Before long, spatial fluctuations appeared at the entrance.
The scout returned.
Every gaze in the hall fell upon him.
His face was pale with shock. He looked at Daniel with unmistakable reverence, then spoke in a trembling voice.

"The Supreme Commander’s report is true. The main Tribulation-Ash Army has been completely destroyed. Only scattered remnants remain in several medium and minor planes. All major Oracle-grade monsters and the central force have been eliminated."
The statement struck the officials like a thunderclap.
Their minds went blank.
Daniel had truly destroyed the entire main army alone.

Could such a feat be accomplished by a single person? He was supposedly only Divine-grade, yet he had completed an undertaking that Governor Loka himself had been unable to attempt. The strength required was beyond their understanding.
Their disbelief transformed into awe, and their attitudes changed with astonishing speed.
"As expected of the Supreme Commander! You created a miracle with a single expedition. Such a record has no equal in the past and may never be surpassed in the future."
"Your strength is greater than any of us imagined. I am completely convinced."
"The Supreme Commander will surely become one of the Eternal Empire’s greatest pillars."
Daniel ignored the flattery and looked directly at Loka.
"Governor, now that I have suppressed the main army, we should determine how the achievement will be recorded."
Loka’s expression tightened.
Daniel continued in an even tone.

"I served as the primary force and destroyed the Tribulation-Ash Army’s central strength. You will lead the local experts in eliminating the remaining monsters and completing the final cleanup. That contribution is also valuable. We will report the operation accordingly. Are you satisfied with this distribution?"
The meaning was unmistakable.

Daniel would claim the overwhelming majority of the merit. Loka and the Uma officials would receive enough credit for the cleanup to avoid complete humiliation, but no one would mistake who had saved the starfield.

Loka was deeply dissatisfied. At the very least, he wanted a share large enough to place him on equal footing with Daniel. Yet he had not participated in the decisive battle, and every person in the hall now knew it.
Arguing would only expose his greed and invite Daniel to exclude him entirely.
After a long silence, Governor Loka nodded.
"That arrangement is reasonable."
With those words, the greatest achievement in the history of the Uma Plane was formally credited to Daniel.

chapters.title: Chapter 468 -468-Entering the Holy See
paragraphs: Every official in the hall heard the exchange between Daniel and Governor Loka.

Their reactions varied. Many were reluctant to accept that almost all the merit would belong to Daniel, while they received only the remnants of the campaign. However, none dared object. Daniel’s earlier execution of the Chief Inspector had already demonstrated how decisively he dealt with resistance. Now he had added an impossible military achievement to that display of authority.
The matter was settled immediately.

Loka prepared an official report describing the destruction of the main Tribulation-Ash Army and the local government’s responsibility for eliminating the survivors. He handed the document to Daniel, who pressed his Supreme Commander’s seal onto it with the token issued by the Holy See.
Once the record was complete, Daniel prepared to leave without delay.

His work in the Heavenly River Starfield was finished. Upon returning to the Holy See, he could use this merit to obtain a permanent imperial appointment. That appointment would grant him Realm-Crosser Points and, even more importantly, a Racial Talent for humanity.
Those rewards were far more attractive than remaining in Uma Plane to listen to local officials flatter him.
Daniel boarded his Emperor-class sacred vessel and set a course for the Imperial City. The ship crossed the starfield at astonishing speed. Before long, the familiar ancient capital appeared ahead.
The moment he entered the city, he went directly to Prince Dorek’s residence.

Dorek still looked thin and somewhat fragile, but the hesitation that had once surrounded him had faded. Daniel briefly explained the result of the mission and instructed him to prepare for the political consequences. Then they waited for the Holy See’s official decree.
"I should be the first realm-crosser to receive a formal position within the Holy See," Daniel thought, his eyes flashing with anticipation.
Dorek, meanwhile, was overwhelmed by the report.
"Teacher truly is invincible within this age," he said with open admiration. "You completed a mission that troubled countless imperial experts as though it were nothing."

The Tribulation-Ash Monsters had driven the local government into despair, yet Daniel had suppressed them without meaningful assistance from a single official of Uma Plane. He had relied entirely upon his own treasures and combat strength.

If Daniel had been a high-stage Oracle-grade expert, the result would still have been impressive. But he was genuinely Divine-grade. The disparity between his Rank and his achievements made the feat almost unbelievable.
Daniel merely smiled at Dorek’s praise.

He knew the victory had not been effortless. He had consumed a significant portion of the Oracle-grade treasures obtained from the Golden Holy Mountain. Their value amounted to an enormous number of mountain points and Origin Crystals. Even with sufficient points, many of those treasures could be acquired only when the mountain happened to possess stock.
Still, the anticipated reward made the expenditure worthwhile.
The Holy See responded quickly.
An imperial envoy arrived at Dorek’s residence and publicly read the Eternal Emperor’s decree. Daniel was granted a formal sixth-rank position: Inspector of the Oracle Hall.
Along with the appointment came several rare materials and a system reward.
[You have obtained 5,000 Realm-Crosser Points!]
Daniel had previously accumulated one hundred points from killing another realm-crosser. With the new reward, his total rose to 5,100.
He immediately opened the points interface.
This time, the larger balance unlocked information that had previously been hidden. At last, he saw the object he had crossed the River of Time to find.
[Great Universal Will Fragment]
[Grade]: Supreme
[Restriction]: Only realm-crossers may use this item.
[Effect]: Upon use, advances the user’s Spacetime Law by one stage.
[Current Location]: Imperial Treasury
[Exchange Price]: 100,000,000 Realm-Crosser Points
Daniel stared at the price.
One hundred million points.

Realm-Crosser Points were restricted by the Great Dao and could not receive Millionfold Boost. Accumulating such a number through official salaries, missions, or kills would be extraordinarily difficult.
Then a smile appeared on his face.
"Now that I know where it is, I no longer need to obtain it through the exchange shop."

The fragment was stored inside the imperial treasury. If Dorek became the next Eternal Emperor, obtaining it would be simple. Daniel would not need to spend a single point. Given Dorek’s trust in him, the prince would almost certainly grant the request.
Daniel had found a far more efficient path.
Dorek, however, was not satisfied with the appointment.
The envoy had barely departed when the prince frowned and began complaining.

"Teacher, something is wrong within the Holy See. With your merit, you should have received a sixth-rank position carrying real authority. Why were you given the title of Inspector of the Oracle Hall?"
He paced across the chamber.

"The Oracle Hall holds a transcendent position within the empire. It is where the Oracle-grade experts gather. An inspector assigned there sounds impressive, but in reality it is an empty office. No ordinary official dares investigate the true powerhouses of the hall."
Dorek’s anger grew.

"Prince Lucian has cultivated in the Oracle Hall since childhood. Someone from his faction may have interfered and replaced the powerful position originally intended for you. Yes, that must be what happened."

Under the original plan, the best outcome would have been Daniel’s entry into the Imperial City Defense system. With his achievement, a single recommendation from the capital’s governor could have placed him in a position controlling troops, investigations, or strategic resources. That would have created a powerful foundation for Dorek’s future struggle.
Even a lesser result should have provided some practical authority.

Dorek had spent enormous resources cultivating contacts within the Holy See. Those connections should have been able to secure a useful sixth-rank post without difficulty. Instead, Daniel had received a dangerous ceremonial appointment.

Prince Lucian was widely believed to be the strongest and most talented of the imperial princes. He had lived and cultivated within the Oracle Hall for years, and many of its experts favored him. To the empire, the Oracle Hall was practically Lucian’s greatest supporting faction.
Daniel belonged to Dorek’s camp. Sending him into Lucian’s territory could hardly be considered a reward.

Worse, the title of inspector did not allow Daniel to supervise the Oracle-grade experts themselves. His authority extended only over the administrative and service organizations assigned to support the Oracle Hall.
In simple terms, he was a high-ranking overseer with no power over the people who truly mattered.
Rather than granting Daniel influence, the position placed him in a vulnerable location where Lucian’s supporters could watch every action he took and manufacture mistakes at will.
Dorek could see only a trap.

Daniel, however, remained calm. The appointment was not what they had expected, but every position created opportunities. If someone had deliberately placed him inside the Oracle Hall’s sphere of influence, he intended to discover why and turn the arrangement against its creator.

chapters.title: Chapter 469 -469-The Racial Talent
paragraphs: Compared with the Oracle Hall itself, Daniel’s new office stood on the weaker side of the relationship.

If the hall wished to create difficulties for him, it could do so with almost no effort. Every report, inspection, and administrative decision could become an excuse for an accusation. That was why Dorek was furious.
Who had interfered with their plan?
Prince Lucian was the most likely suspect. Among the princes, he possessed the strongest connection to the Oracle Hall and the greatest ability to influence appointments related to it.
Daniel, however, showed no anxiety. He had already begun considering how to use the position.
Before he could explain, a system notification sounded in his ears.
[Notice: You may now select a Racial Talent.]

[You may designate any talent ability you currently possess as the Racial Talent. Every individual belonging to your race will gain the corresponding talent. You will retain complete control over it and may grant or revoke the talent from any chosen individual.]
[Alternatively, you may randomly draw a new talent. The selected talent will be obtained immediately by you and every member of your race.]
[Please choose the method by which the Racial Talent will be acquired.]
Daniel immediately understood the two options.

The first method allowed him to choose an ability he already possessed and share it with all humanity. Its greatest advantage was control. He could decide who received the talent, who was excluded, and whose access would be revoked. It would give him an extraordinary degree of authority over the entire human race.
The disadvantage was that Daniel himself would gain no new benefit. He already possessed the chosen talent.

The second method was a random draw. It would create a completely new talent and grant it to Daniel as well as every human. If the result were powerful, Daniel’s own strength and humanity’s potential would rise together.
The risk was obvious.
A random talent could be useless. If the system produced a weak or highly specialized ability, the opportunity would be wasted permanently.
Daniel considered the matter only briefly before choosing the first option.
Humanity needed a reliable foundation more than he needed a gamble.
"For the current human race, the most suitable talent is the War God Physique."
He confirmed the selection.
The War God Physique became humanity’s Racial Talent.
At that same moment, throughout the Myriad-Race Cosmos, a brilliant notification rang in the ears of every human player.
[Ding! Player Daniel has designated his talent ability, War God Physique, as the Human Racial Talent!]
[Ding! Congratulations to all human players. You have obtained the Racial Talent: War God Physique!]
At first, most players were confused. Then they opened their talent panels and read the new ability.
Their eyes widened.
Hearts began pounding across countless worlds.
"What is this? I feel as though my combat potential just exploded!"
"Daniel is truly the eternal god of humanity. He actually shared a talent of this level with everyone!"
"No wonder he has always been so powerful. He possessed something this terrifying from the beginning. Now we can finally benefit from it too!"
"My attributes, recovery, and battle instincts have all improved. This is absurd!"

Excited discussions flooded every player channel. Guilds began recalculating their combat formations. Lone players rushed toward dangerous regions they had previously avoided. Entire human factions suddenly possessed far greater confidence in competing against the other races.
Daniel, separated from them by another era and spacetime, naturally heard none of those reactions.
For him, the decision was strategic.

The War God Physique would raise the strength of every human player. Stronger players meant a stronger faction, greater territorial expansion, and more resources flowing toward the civilization he controlled. Furthermore, Daniel could revoke the talent at will. Anyone who betrayed humanity or opposed him could lose the gift instantly.
The Racial Talent strengthened the human race while also increasing Daniel’s control over it.
For his next opportunity, however, he intended to choose the random method.
"This selection provides a secure foundation. Next time, I can afford to gamble on a new talent. Perhaps the result will be exceptional."
Once the process was complete, Daniel returned his attention to Dorek.
The prince was still visibly angry about the Holy See’s decree.

Daniel also believed that someone had acted against him, but political hostility had become ordinary. In a succession struggle, every faction attempted to obstruct the others. Minor sabotage was almost polite compared with the assassinations already launched against him.
The only uncertain question was whether Prince Lucian had personally arranged the appointment.
After considering it, Daniel decided the answer did not matter. Whoever had placed him in the position had also given him a legitimate reason to enter the Oracle Hall. He would use that opportunity.
"You still seem angry," Daniel said.
Dorek gritted his teeth.
"Teacher, you are the foundation of my entire faction. How could I not be angry? If anything happens to you, I am finished."
He stepped closer, his voice filled with urgency.

"Now that you have accepted the appointment, they can attack you regardless of what you do. If you act, they will accuse you of exceeding your authority. If you do nothing, they will accuse you of neglecting your duties. They need only identify a few supposed errors in your inspections to implicate our entire faction."
Dorek’s expression grew increasingly severe.
"A stain upon your record becomes a stain upon all of us. They could use it to declare that our faction lacks the qualifications to compete for the throne. How can I remain calm?"
As he spoke, his anxiety rose. Yet when he looked at Daniel’s completely composed face, his own anger gradually faded.
"Teacher, why are you not worried? Have you already found a way to break the trap?"
Daniel smiled and shrugged.
"Do not waste any opportunity. Since I now possess this ceremonial office, I also possess a lawful reason to investigate the Oracle Hall."
Dorek was startled.

"Teacher, the Oracle Hall is Prince Lucian’s territory. You may not fully understand how dangerous it is. Almost every Oracle-grade expert serving the empire has some connection to that place, including numerous high-stage Oracle-grade powerhouses. Its internal relationships are more complicated than those of the imperial court itself. The empire’s foundation was built around it."
He continued hurriedly.

"Lucian possesses the greatest cultivation talent among all the princes. He is also the strongest. He has already reached the peak of Divine-grade and may break through to Oracle-grade at any moment. If you enter the Oracle Hall alone, he and his supporters will certainly target you."
Dorek looked at Daniel with genuine concern.
"Please reconsider."

Daniel understood the fear behind those words. The entire Dorek faction now depended upon him. None of them wanted their greatest strategist and strongest hidden pillar to walk voluntarily into the heart of an enemy camp.
But Daniel had no intention of avoiding danger merely because others believed it existed.
The Oracle Hall might be Lucian’s foundation.
That was precisely why Daniel wanted to enter it.

sentences.text: Compared with the Oracle Hall itself, Daniel’s new office stood on the weaker side of the relationship.
If the hall wished to create difficulties for him, it could do so with almost no effort.
Every report, inspection, and administrative decision could become an excuse for an accusation.
That was why Dorek was furious.
Who had interfered with their plan?
Prince Lucian was the most likely suspect.
Among the princes, he possessed the strongest connection to the Oracle Hall and the greatest ability to influence appointments related to it.
Daniel, however, showed no anxiety.
He had already begun considering how to use the position.
Before he could explain, a system notification sounded in his ears.
[Notice: You may now select a Racial Talent.]
[You may designate any talent ability you currently possess as the Racial Talent.
Every individual belonging to your race will gain the corresponding talent.
You will retain complete control over it and may grant or revoke the talent from any chosen individual.]
[Alternatively, you may randomly draw a new talent.
The selected talent will be obtained immediately by you and every member of your race.]
[Please choose the method by which the Racial Talent will be acquired.]
Daniel immediately understood the two options.
The first method allowed him to choose an ability he already possessed and share it with all humanity.
Its greatest advantage was control.
He could decide who received the talent, who was excluded, and whose access would be revoked.
It would give him an extraordinary degree of authority over the entire human race.
The disadvantage was that Daniel himself would gain no new benefit.
He already possessed the chosen talent.
The second method was a random draw.
It would create a completely new talent and grant it to Daniel as well as every human.
If the result were powerful, Daniel’s own strength and humanity’s potential would rise together.
The risk was obvious.
A random talent could be useless.
If the system produced a weak or highly specialized ability, the opportunity would be wasted permanently.
Daniel considered the matter only briefly before choosing the first option.
Humanity needed a reliable foundation more than he needed a gamble.
"For the current human race, the most suitable talent is the War God Physique."
He confirmed the selection.
The War God Physique became humanity’s Racial Talent.
At that same moment, throughout the Myriad-Race Cosmos, a brilliant notification rang in the ears of every human player.
[Ding!
Player Daniel has designated his talent ability, War God Physique, as the Human Racial Talent!]
[Ding!
Congratulations to all human players.
You have obtained the Racial Talent: War God Physique!]
At first, most players were confused.
Then they opened their talent panels and read the new ability.
Their eyes widened.
Hearts began pounding across countless worlds.
"What is this?
I feel as though my combat potential just exploded!"
"Daniel is truly the eternal god of humanity.
He actually shared a talent of this level with everyone!"
"No wonder he has always been so powerful.
He possessed something this terrifying from the beginning.
Now we can finally benefit from it too!"
"My attributes, recovery, and battle instincts have all improved.
This is absurd!"
Excited discussions flooded every player channel.
Guilds began recalculating their combat formations.
Lone players rushed toward dangerous regions they had previously avoided.
Entire human factions suddenly possessed far greater confidence in competing against the other races.
Daniel, separated from them by another era and spacetime, naturally heard none of those reactions.
For him, the decision was strategic.
The War God Physique would raise the strength of every human player.
Stronger players meant a stronger faction, greater territorial expansion, and more resources flowing toward the civilization he controlled.
Furthermore, Daniel could revoke the talent at will.
Anyone who betrayed humanity or opposed him could lose the gift instantly.
The Racial Talent strengthened the human race while also increasing Daniel’s control over it.
For his next opportunity, however, he intended to choose the random method.
"This selection provides a secure foundation.
Next time, I can afford to gamble on a new talent.
Perhaps the result will be exceptional."
Once the process was complete, Daniel returned his attention to Dorek.
The prince was still visibly angry about the Holy See’s decree.
Daniel also believed that someone had acted against him, but political hostility had become ordinary.
In a succession struggle, every faction attempted to obstruct the others.
Minor sabotage was almost polite compared with the assassinations already launched against him.
The only uncertain question was whether Prince Lucian had personally arranged the appointment.
After considering it, Daniel decided the answer did not matter.
Whoever had placed him in the position had also given him a legitimate reason to enter the Oracle Hall.
He would use that opportunity.
"You still seem angry," Daniel said.
Dorek gritted his teeth.
"Teacher, you are the foundation of my entire faction.
How could I not be angry?
If anything happens to you, I am finished."
He stepped closer, his voice filled with urgency.
"Now that you have accepted the appointment, they can attack you regardless of what you do.
If you act, they will accuse you of exceeding your authority.
If you do nothing, they will accuse you of neglecting your duties.
They need only identify a few supposed errors in your inspections to implicate our entire faction."
Dorek’s expression grew increasingly severe.
"A stain upon your record becomes a stain upon all of us.
They could use it to declare that our faction lacks the qualifications to compete for the throne.
How can I remain calm?"
As he spoke, his anxiety rose.
Yet when he looked at Daniel’s completely composed face, his own anger gradually faded.
"Teacher, why are you not worried?
Have you already found a way to break the trap?"

Since I now possess this ceremonial office, I also possess a lawful reason to investigate the Oracle Hall."

chapters.title: Chapter 470 -470-Entering the Oracle Hall
paragraphs: Daniel silently nodded after hearing Dorek’s warning.

He understood why the prince was worried. Every member of Dorek’s faction now regarded Daniel as their greatest support. If he suffered an accident inside the Oracle Hall, the entire political structure they had built might collapse overnight.
But Daniel did not believe anything inside the hall could truly threaten him.
"My purpose in going there is simple," he said. "I want to see whether I can shake Prince Lucian’s foundation."
Dorek listened closely.

"The force capable of interfering with the imperial appointment and changing my expected position into Inspector of the Oracle Hall must possess considerable influence. If Lucian arranged it, then I will make him taste the consequences of his own scheme."
A cold smile appeared on Daniel’s face.

"If another prince manipulated the appointment instead, then that person clearly hopes Lucian and I will fight until both sides are weakened. No matter which of us suffers, the hidden faction will benefit. Every prince has dangerous figures supporting him, so I must enter the Oracle Hall and discover who created this situation."
He waved a hand dismissively.
"You do not need to worry. Nothing will happen to me."
Daniel’s confidence finally eased some of Dorek’s anxiety.

The Oracle Hall was not physically located inside the Imperial City, yet it could be reached from almost any point within the capital. It existed inside an enormous secret realm personally created by the Eternal Emperor.

That realm was larger than many great worlds. The Eternal Emperor had stood at the peak of half-step Eternal when he opened it, so both its stability and scale surpassed ordinary planes and secret regions by an unimaginable degree.
Daniel’s new office came with a corresponding inspection token. By activating it, he could enter the secret realm directly.
He did not hesitate.
Divine power flowed into the token. Space folded around him, and in the next instant, Daniel appeared within the realm of the Oracle Hall.

A towering sacred mountain dominated the world before him. It was so vast that it seemed to occupy the entire horizon. Palaces, ancient paths, and law formations covered its slopes, while the highest peaks disappeared into clouds filled with divine radiance.
Yet the majesty of the scene could not conceal the corruption.
Daniel immediately sensed an extraordinarily dense aura of tribulation ash.

Even a shallow breath drew gray particles into his body. The Great Dao Tribulation Source planted within him responded to the surrounding fluctuations, and thin traces of ash began appearing across his skin.
Daniel had expected the Oracle Hall to suffer severe tribulation-ash corruption, but the reality exceeded his estimate.

This was the gathering place of the empire’s Oracle-grade experts. The stronger a cultivator became, the more rapidly the declining Great Dao corrupted them. Outside the imperial palace itself, there was probably no location in the Eternal Empire more heavily contaminated than this realm.
Daniel did not remain still.

He moved toward the central mountain. With every step closer, the air grew more repulsive. The scent was not merely physical decay. It carried the sensation of laws weakening and the Great Dao rotting from within.

Powerful formations and restrictions surrounded the outer regions of the Oracle Hall. Daniel’s inspection token opened each barrier automatically, allowing him to pass through layers that would have stopped ordinary Divine-grade experts instantly.

When he reached the base of the sacred mountain, an invisible force descended and pressed him from the sky. Flight was prohibited. Anyone entering the core region had to climb the mountain path on foot.
Daniel landed and began ascending.
Layers of tribulation ash covered the stone steps, palace roofs, and ancient statues. There was almost no living color anywhere.
Countless servants swept the ash day and night. Yet every section they cleaned was covered again almost immediately. Their work never ended.
None of them reacted to Daniel’s arrival. They moved mechanically, neither looking toward him nor speaking.
"Puppets," Daniel murmured. "Every one of them is a Divine-grade puppet."

As he climbed, he saw one puppet suddenly freeze. Long exposure to tribulation ash had corrupted its body and damaged the laws controlling it. Several nearby puppets immediately approached, lifted the broken servant, and carried it away.
Their duties clearly included more than cleaning the mountain. They also removed companions that had become too corrupted to function.
Daniel continued upward until he reached a checkpoint guarded by living experts. He displayed the Inspector Token and passed without difficulty.
The moment he entered the inner hall, a low-stage Oracle-grade expert appeared directly in front of him.
"You are the newly appointed inspector?"
Daniel studied the man.

The Oracle-grade expert’s gaze shifted constantly. His expression was tense, and even his voice trembled slightly. He looked less like someone questioning a subordinate and more like an actor waiting for a signal.
Daniel frowned and prepared to answer.
Before he could speak, the man suddenly threw himself onto the floor. His face twisted into an exaggerated expression of pain and terror.
"What is the meaning of this? You have only just taken office, yet you attacked me without reason! This matter is extremely serious. You will not leave the Oracle Hall today!"
Daniel almost laughed.

It was a crude attempt at framing him, the sort of trick commonly used by petty criminals and corrupt officials. He had not expected to encounter such a ridiculous performance inside the empire’s most revered sacred institution.

"Stop acting," Daniel said coldly. "I am merely Divine-grade, while you are a second-stage Oracle-grade expert. If I claimed to have injured you, do you believe anyone would accept it? End this farce while you still can."
The man remained on the floor, clutching his chest and pretending to struggle for breath.

"If another Divine-grade official attacked me, no one would believe it. But you are the genius who destroyed the Tribulation-Ash Army alone. Everyone in the Oracle Hall has heard that you can defeat enemies above your Rank. It is perfectly reasonable that you could injure me."
Daniel was briefly speechless.

His reputation had spread through the Oracle Hall more quickly than he had imagined. The very achievement that protected his political position was now being used to make the false accusation appear plausible.
A cold smile slowly formed on his face.
He raised his hand.
"Your performance is too poor. Why don’t I help you turn the false injury into a real one?"
The Oracle-grade expert’s expression changed instantly.
"What are you doing? This is the Oracle Hall! How dare you cause trouble here?"

Daniel glanced toward the distance. Several Oracle-grade auras were approaching. They might have been waiting nearby from the beginning, or they might have responded to the staged commotion. Either way, the trap was obvious.
He did not lower his hand.
Law light gathered in his palm.

"You accuse me of creating disorder, yet you deliberately arranged this pathetic scheme the moment I arrived. Since you have already decided that I attacked you, I may as well make your accusation true."
The approaching experts saw Daniel preparing to strike and shouted furiously.
"Bastard! What do you think you are doing?"
They were too late.
Golden light flashed.
The Holy Spirit Stone crossed the hall and pierced directly through the low-stage Oracle-grade expert’s shoulder.
Blood erupted across the floor.
"Aaaah!"
The man who had been pretending moments earlier finally released a genuine scream of agony.
Daniel looked down at him without sympathy.
Inside the Oracle Hall, his first lesson had already become clear.
The people targeting him expected restraint.
They had chosen the wrong opponent.

chapters.title: Chapter 471 -471-Intimidation
paragraphs: The Oracle-grade experts who had just arrived were furious.

The Oracle Hall held a position of supreme honor within the Eternal Empire. It was one of the pillars supporting the dynasty and the gathering place of its greatest cultivators. No one dared create disorder inside its sacred grounds, much less attack one of its members.
Yet Daniel had just wounded an Oracle-grade expert in front of them.
Daniel faced their anger with open disdain.

"The Oracle Hall calls itself a sacred institution, yet the first thing it does to a newly appointed inspector is arrange such a shameless trap. If this matter becomes public, will the hall still have the dignity to call itself holy?"
His gaze sharpened.
"What now? Do the rest of you intend to arrest me?"
One expert’s face turned dark with rage.

"You attacked a member of the Oracle Hall. Why shouldn’t we seize you? I do not care who you serve. Anyone who harms one of our experts must answer to the hall. Even an imperial prince would be judged, much less a minor sixth-rank official like you."
Daniel calmly took out a crystal sphere.
It was an image-recording artifact capable of preserving everything that had occurred around it.
"Is that so? Then what will happen if I reveal this recording to the entire empire?"
A cold laugh escaped him.
"High-stage Oracle-grade experts can reverse spacetime and observe the truth directly. They will know exactly what happened here. When that moment comes, who will be judged?"
Daniel stepped forward.
"Or perhaps I should ask a different question. Who ordered you to create this incident and damage the reputation of the Oracle Hall? Are you still certain you want to take me away?"
The experts fell silent.

Daniel had reversed the situation with a few questions. They had acted according to a plan and knew they possessed no legal or moral advantage. Their only accusation was that Daniel had genuinely wounded the man on the floor, but the attack had occurred only after an obvious attempt to frame him.
If the dispute reached the upper levels of the Oracle Hall, a powerful expert could reconstruct every moment through spacetime. The truth would be impossible to hide.
The group began communicating through Divine Sense.
"What should we do? His argument is difficult to refute. If this becomes a major investigation, the high-stage experts will discover everything immediately."
"Are we really going to fight him to the end over this? It does not seem worthwhile."
"We should stop here. Continuing will only expose the people behind us."
They reached an agreement quickly.
Without another word, they helped the injured low-stage Oracle-grade expert to his feet. Before leaving, they glared at Daniel, but their retreat resembled that of defeated dogs.
Daniel had predicted the outcome correctly. If the incident expanded, the Oracle Hall itself would lose prestige, while the conspirators would face severe punishment for abusing its name.
Elsewhere in the secret realm, the confrontation was being observed.
Inside a secluded cultivation residence, a noble young man stood before a wall of light. The scene of Daniel intimidating the Oracle-grade experts played across its surface.
Beside the young man stood a masked powerhouse.
Prince Lucian waved his hand and erased the image.
"Teacher Luen, what do you think?"
Luen’s voice was low and thoughtful.
"Whatever his true combat strength may be, his intelligence is no weaker than mine. I cannot determine which future era produced such a figure."
Lucian smiled bitterly, envy visible in his eyes.
"Dorek truly possesses extraordinary luck. He somehow obtained the assistance of a man like this."
He began listing Daniel’s achievements.

"Daniel brought Dorek safely back to the Imperial City and placed him near the center of power. He established contact with the Fated Human Race and secured their support. He planned the restaurant incident that brought Dorek directly into Father’s sight. Now he has single-handedly suppressed the Tribulation-Ash Army of the Heavenly River Starfield."
Lucian sighed.
"Every action proves his ability. His importance to Dorek is almost equal to your importance to me."
Luen shook his head.

"The high-stage Oracle-grade realm-crossers who descended into this era are all suppressed by the local Great Dao. We can display only a fraction of our true power. Even under those conditions, Daniel has performed extraordinarily well."
He paused.
"To eliminate the Tribulation-Ash Army alone would require a substantial price even from me."
Lucian’s expression became grave.
"If he continues strengthening Dorek’s faction, they will become one of our greatest rivals. How should we deal with them?"
Luen gave a helpless smile.

"Honestly, I have not found a reliable method. Instead of concentrating upon eliminating Dorek and Daniel, we should increase our own foundations. Only when our faction forms an unstoppable trend will we cease fearing individual experts."
He explained his reasoning carefully.

"Daniel and Dorek do not make obvious mistakes. They do not merely survive crises; they transform danger into profit. The more schemes we launch against them, the more opportunities we create for ourselves to fail. A direct confrontation would benefit other princes."
Luen turned toward Lucian.

"For now, improving your strength is the correct path. Alvin has already brought much of the Holy See under his influence, while Dorek has begun penetrating it through his own network. We can imitate them, recruit powerful officials, and expand our control instead of wasting resources on reckless attacks."
Meanwhile, Daniel continued deeper into the Oracle Hall.
After intimidating the conspirators, he followed the mountain path without further obstruction.
Then space around him suddenly reversed.
The hall vanished.

In the next instant, Daniel found himself standing in a vast wilderness filled with life. Spiritual beasts ran among green hills. Rare herbs and divine plants swayed beneath a gentle wind. White clouds crossed a clear blue sky, and a faint fragrance filled the air.
Before him floated an enormous transparent chessboard.
Two forces occupied it.
One represented tribulation ash. The other represented living beings.
The Tribulation-Ash side controlled most of the board. The living side had been pushed to the edge and was only a few moves away from complete corruption and defeat.
It was now the living side’s turn.
Daniel did not immediately study the pieces. He focused upon the world around him.
"Where is this?"
He had been inside the Oracle Hall only a moment earlier.
Golden light flashed through his eyes as he examined the laws of the region.
Soon, he saw the truth.
"This entire place is an illusion."
The illusion was far beyond ordinary Sacred Arts. Only a high-stage Oracle-grade powerhouse of at least T7 could have created such a complete false world.
Daniel looked toward the chessboard again.
Who within the Oracle Hall possessed both the power and authority to bring him here without warning?
The answer was already beginning to form in his mind.

Even under those conditions, Daniel has performed extraordinarily well."
He paused.
"To eliminate the Tribulation-Ash Army alone would require a substantial price even from me."
Lucian’s expression became grave.
"If he continues strengthening Dorek’s faction, they will become one of our greatest rivals.
How should we deal with them?"
Luen gave a helpless smile.
"Honestly, I have not found a reliable method.
Instead of concentrating upon eliminating Dorek and Daniel, we should increase our own foundations.
Only when our faction forms an unstoppable trend will we cease fearing individual experts."
He explained his reasoning carefully.
"Daniel and Dorek do not make obvious mistakes.
They do not merely survive crises; they transform danger into profit.
The more schemes we launch against them, the more opportunities we create for ourselves to fail.
A direct confrontation would benefit other princes."
Luen turned toward Lucian.
"For now, improving your strength is the correct path.
Alvin has already brought much of the Holy See under his influence, while Dorek has begun penetrating it through his own network.
We can imitate them, recruit powerful officials, and expand our control instead of wasting resources on reckless attacks."
Meanwhile, Daniel continued deeper into the Oracle Hall.
After intimidating the conspirators, he followed the mountain path without further obstruction.
Then space around him suddenly reversed.
The hall vanished.
In the next instant, Daniel found himself standing in a vast wilderness filled with life.
Spiritual beasts ran among green hills.
Rare herbs and divine plants swayed beneath a gentle wind.
White clouds crossed a clear blue sky, and a faint fragrance filled the air.
Before him floated an enormous transparent chessboard.
Two forces occupied it.
One represented tribulation ash.
The other represented living beings.
The Tribulation-Ash side controlled most of the board.
The living side had been pushed to the edge and was only a few moves away from complete corruption and defeat.
It was now the living side’s turn.
Daniel did not immediately study the pieces.
He focused upon the world around him.
"Where is this?"
He had been inside the Oracle Hall only a moment earlier.
Golden light flashed through his eyes as he examined the laws of the region.
Soon, he saw the truth.
"This entire place is an illusion."
The illusion was far beyond ordinary Sacred Arts.
Only a high-stage Oracle-grade powerhouse of at least T7 could have created such a complete false world.
Daniel looked toward the chessboard again.
Who within the Oracle Hall possessed both the power and authority to bring him here without warning?
The answer was already beginning to form in his mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 472 -472-The Master of the Oracle Hall
paragraphs: "This place is unquestionably an illusion."
Daniel studied the enormous chessboard floating before him.

Its arrangement felt strangely familiar. The more closely he examined the two opposing sides, the more certain he became that the illusion had been created by the master of the Oracle Hall, the T9 Oracle-grade expert who stood at the peak of the institution.
The chessboard was probably a test.

The Tribulation-Ash faction and the faction of living beings were clearly separated. One represented decay and inevitable extinction. The other represented the fragile civilizations still struggling to survive.
"Is he testing how I would respond to the threat of tribulation-ash corruption?"
Daniel considered the current condition of the universe.

The source of the Great Dao was already declining. Tribulation-ash corruption was no longer a temporary disaster that could be eliminated by killing a few monsters. It had become the direction of the age itself.
Changing emperors would not stop that process.

No matter who inherited the throne, the universe would continue decaying. Its lifespan was nearing the end. The true concern of the highest-level experts was no longer merely who would rule the Eternal Empire, but whether any life would remain to be ruled.
Daniel’s thoughts grew clearer.

The Eternal Emperor possessed only a small chance of surviving the coming tribulation. If he failed, nothing would prevent the continuing spread of tribulation ash. The next emperor’s first and greatest responsibility would be to lead the universe’s living beings toward a path of survival.
The chessboard asked how that path should be found.

It was formed from a law-based Sacred Art. There were no written rules and no need to calculate ordinary moves. Daniel only needed to immerse his consciousness in the board, and the problem would reveal itself.
He extended his Divine Sense.
The illusion changed instantly.

Endless Tribulation-Ash Monsters appeared before him. They covered the horizon like a final catastrophe, destroying worlds and converting every living creature they encountered. The lands behind them were gray, silent, and filled with the scent of decay.

The region around Daniel remained green and vibrant, overflowing with spiritual energy. Yet its survival was temporary. The ash tide continued approaching, and every possible defense seemed destined to fail.
What move could save the living side?
Daniel withdrew his consciousness.
A cold smile appeared on his face.
"Why should I solve the game according to its assumptions?"
The black Divine Spear materialized beside him. Law power erupted throughout the illusion.
"Shatter."
Daniel seized the spear and struck the chessboard with all his strength.
"If the universe is destined to die, then abandon it. There is no reason to remain trapped by the question of how life can survive inside a world that cannot be saved."
The spear descended.
"Leave this universe. Find another plane, another cosmos, or another home. Instead of sacrificing everyone to preserve a dying shell, take those willing to depart and begin again elsewhere."
Boom!

The chessboard exploded beneath the Divine Spear. Transparent fragments scattered across the sky and dissolved into law light. The entire structure was destroyed so completely that it could not restore itself.
Space rotated around Daniel.
When his vision stabilized, he had returned to the Oracle Hall.
A distant, ethereal voice sounded in his ears.
"Friend, would you be willing to meet me?"
The voice carried deep exhaustion and the weight of countless years.
"Yes," Daniel answered.
A terrifying law enveloped him. His body disappeared from the hall before the surrounding space had time to tremble.
He reappeared inside a quiet residence located in a remote plane.
A lush tree stood in the courtyard. Beneath it sat a white-haired old man. A carved stone table separated two seats, and two cups of hot tea released thin streams of steam.
The old man faced away from Daniel.
"You have traveled far, friend. Please sit and rest."
Daniel approached without hesitation and took the empty seat.
Only then did he see the old man’s face clearly.

The elder had white brows and a long white beard. His expression was gentle, almost grandfatherly, but the aura within his body was vast beyond measure. He was a T9 Oracle-grade powerhouse who had already reached the peak of the tier. Only a single step separated him from an even greater realm.
At the same time, the tribulation-ash corruption surrounding him was terrifyingly dense.
Daniel instinctively frowned and held his breath. It did little good. The decaying aura affected Divine Sense directly and did not require physical inhalation.
"Drink the tea," the elder said, gesturing toward the cup.
Daniel considered the offer for a moment, then lifted the cup and took a sip.
Information exploded inside his mind.
In only an instant, he obtained a complete Sacred Art.
He examined it with Divine Sense and was genuinely surprised by its grade.
[Sacred Seal]
[Grade]: High Divine-grade
[Type]: All-Purpose
[Restriction]: Divine-grade or above
[Effects]:

In its ordinary form, the Sacred Seal may mobilize all Strength contained within the user’s sage-rank domain through a unified Sacred Art. In its Oracle-grade form, the divided seals may perfectly release one hundred percent of the user’s available Strength through this Sacred Art.
[Description]: A supreme integration of multiple Sacred Arts. Extremely rare.
Daniel had received a top-tier Sacred Art by drinking a single mouthful of tea.

From the nature of the technique, he suspected the old man had created or modified it specifically for him. Daniel did not reject such generosity, nor did he waste time asking why the gift had been offered.
"Thank you, Senior."
The elder studied him for a long moment.
"I once considered the same solution you chose," he said. "I thought about abandoning this universe and searching for a new home."
His eyes became distant.

"At that time, tribulation-ash corruption was far less severe. Many forces opposed the idea of leaving. They believed the universe could still be saved, or they refused to surrender the territories, authority, and history they possessed here."
The old man sighed.
"Even now, when destruction is so close, many powers continue to resist evacuation. Until they see the final collapse with their own eyes, they will not willingly leave."
He looked directly at Daniel.
"Do you have a method for dealing with them?"
Daniel smiled. A fierce light appeared in his eyes.
"Those who insist upon remaining may remain. We will take the people willing to leave. When existence itself is at stake, even splitting the entire empire is acceptable."
The elder’s gaze changed.
Daniel had not offered compromise, persuasion, or endless delay.
He had offered a decision.

chapters.title: Chapter 473 -473-The Solution
paragraphs: The old man nodded slowly after hearing Daniel’s answer.

He had clearly considered the same ruthless solution before, but too many concerns had restrained him. He carried the weight of the Oracle Hall, the Eternal Empire, and countless factions that would accuse him of betrayal if he openly suggested abandoning the universe. In that respect, he was far less decisive than Daniel.
"You possess the bearing of a true sovereign," the elder said. "If you were an imperial prince, the others would have no chance of competing with you."
Daniel answered without hesitation.
"Prince Dorek is no less capable than I am. He possesses the qualities of an enlightened ruler and is worth supporting."

He deliberately redirected the conversation toward Dorek. The old man had tried to conceal his identity, but Daniel was almost certain that he was the master of the Oracle Hall and the strongest expert within it.
A statement from this man could influence the entire institution’s position in the succession struggle.
The elder did not answer Daniel’s implied question directly.
"What do you think of Prince Lucian?"
He returned the question with practiced ease, asking Daniel to reveal his judgment first. The choice itself showed that the elder leaned, at least slightly, toward Lucian.
Daniel smiled coldly.
"Prince Lucian is certainly impressive. However..."
"However what?" the elder asked.
"He failed to choose me as his chief minister," Daniel replied. "Therefore, he will lose the succession struggle."
The elder raised an eyebrow. Even with his calm temperament, he found the claim arrogant.
"Would you say the same if the Oracle Hall gave Prince Lucian its full support?"
Daniel shook his head.
"The result would remain unchanged. The Oracle Hall’s support cannot determine the final outcome by itself."
He rested one hand on the stone table.

"The simplest factor is the Eternal Emperor’s attitude, yet that attitude is also the most difficult to understand. Sometimes the greatest advantage becomes the greatest weakness. If the Emperor truly approves of Lucian, then Lucian can inherit the throne even without the Oracle Hall. If the Emperor does not approve of him, the support of every expert in this institution will still fail to change the result."
A faint curve appeared at the corner of Daniel’s mouth.
"Besides, if you had already decided to support Lucian with all your strength, you would not have invited me here."
The elder’s intentions had been exposed completely.
He looked at Daniel for a long time and finally sighed.
"Prince Dorek’s ability to obtain your assistance is indeed an extraordinary opportunity. With you beside him, he will certainly become one of the strongest candidates for the next imperial throne."
Then the elder smiled.
"As for Prince Lucian, I can promise only this: most experts of the Oracle Hall will remain observers. They will not personally enter the succession struggle on his behalf."
Daniel’s eyes brightened.
The statement represented far more than personal neutrality. As master of the Oracle Hall, the old man had revealed the position he intended to impose upon the institution.

Most of Lucian’s apparent foundations came from his years of cultivation inside the hall. If its Oracle-grade experts were forbidden from openly supporting him, the resources he could mobilize would fall close to zero. He would be left with only the personal relationships he had accumulated during his time there.
With a single promise, the prince who had appeared to possess the greatest institutional advantage became one of the weakest competitors.
Daniel’s journey had produced an enormous return.
He rose from his seat.
"On Prince Dorek’s behalf, I thank you, Senior."
The master of the Oracle Hall smiled bitterly.

"Compared with the destruction facing this universe, a struggle for political power is insignificant. I ask only that if Dorek becomes the next Eternal Emperor, you remember the purpose discussed here and help us escape the coming extinction."
Daniel nodded.
"Naturally. When that day arrives, I will remind Dorek of the crisis and ensure that he understands what must be done."
His figure disappeared from the secluded plane.
Daniel left as suddenly as he had arrived. Apart from a small number of powerful observers, no one knew what he had obtained during his visit to the Oracle Hall.
After returning to the outer region of the secret realm, he drew in a deep breath.
"This trip was more profitable than expected. I obtained a top-tier Sacred Art and removed the Oracle Hall as an active force supporting Lucian. Dorek’s path has become much smoother."
Daniel activated the Inspector Token and returned directly to the Imperial City. From there, he made his way back toward Dorek’s residence.
At the same time, Prince Lucian received a new order from the master of the Oracle Hall.
Unless an urgent institutional matter required otherwise, Oracle-grade experts belonging to the hall were forbidden from leaving and interfering in external affairs.
Lucian was stunned.

Daniel had entered the Oracle Hall only a short time earlier, yet the master had already issued a command that effectively cut Lucian off from his greatest source of support. No one knew what understanding the two had reached, but the political result was disastrous for him.
Obtaining the hall’s full support had become almost impossible.
Lucian turned anxiously toward the masked expert beside him.
"Teacher Luen, what should we do? Daniel must have said something to the hall master. I have lost my greatest advantage and may now be the weakest prince remaining in the succession struggle."
Luen showed no panic.
"There is no need to rush. We still possess many options. Your greatest advantage has never been the Oracle Hall. It is your own cultivation."
He looked steadily at Lucian.

"If you successfully break through to Oracle-grade, none of the other princes can compare with you personally. You have already reached the peak of Divine-grade. The final step should not be difficult."
Luen continued in a calm voice.
"Leave external affairs to me. Concentrate upon your breakthrough. Strength remains the most reliable foundation."
Lucian nodded.
"I understand. I will enter seclusion immediately and attempt to reach Oracle-grade."
Yet before he could fully withdraw from the political world, a far greater event shook the Imperial City.
The Eternal Emperor, the half-step Eternal ruler who had dominated the empire for countless years, was finally preparing to face his tribulation.
The succession struggle was no longer a distant contest.
Its final stage had begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 474 -474-The Tribulation Begins
paragraphs: The Eternal Emperor was approaching complete tribulation-ash corruption.

Even an existence at the peak of half-step Eternal could not escape the decline of the Great Dao. Unless he completed his tribulation and broke through to the Eternal realm before the corruption consumed him, he would eventually lose himself and become a Tribulation-Ash Monster.
Only true Eternal power could transcend the decay of the universe.

Unfortunately, the Emperor had not chosen the timing of the tribulation. It had descended upon him before he could complete all the preparations normally required for such an attempt. His treasures, formations, and contingency plans were far from perfect.
Almost every major expert believed his chances of success were extremely small.
The Eternal Emperor himself apparently agreed. In recent days, he had begun arranging matters that would take effect after his death. The most urgent question was the selection of the next ruler.
He still had not named a single crown prince.
That did not surprise the political factions. What surprised them was that, at the final moment, the Emperor appointed two princes to share the responsibilities normally held by one heir.
The first was Dorek.
According to the new decree, Prince Dorek would control every matter related to the imperial legions. He received supreme authority over military appointments, deployments, and strategic commands.
The second was Prince Alvin.
Alvin would manage the empire’s civil administration and every major political matter unrelated to the legions.
The Eternal Emperor had divided the duties of a crown prince into two halves.
Military authority belonged to Dorek.
Civil authority belonged to Alvin.
The decree effectively eliminated every other prince from serious competition. Only Dorek and Alvin retained the qualifications to fight for the throne.
Many experts found the arrangement dangerous. Dividing civil and military power between rival heirs created an obvious risk that the empire itself would split into opposing camps.
Yet the Eternal Emperor had made the choice deliberately. No one believed he had acted without purpose.
The entire Imperial City changed overnight.
Officials, noble clans, military families, and ancient factions began reevaluating their loyalties. Those who had supported other princes felt their hearts sink.
Inside Prince Kane’s residence, expensive treasures shattered one after another.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Kane hurled divine ornaments, ancient vessels, and priceless decorations against the floor.
"Damn it! Why wasn’t I chosen?"
His hair hung loose around his face, and jealousy twisted his features.
"Why does Dorek control the military? In what way am I inferior to him? My cultivation, talent, and intelligence should all surpass his! That position should belong to me. I refuse to accept this!"
Beneath the rage lay fear.

Kane had previously dispatched experts to assassinate Dorek. If Dorek became emperor, he would never forgive those attempts. Kane could expect neither exile nor imprisonment. His end would be complete destruction.
The thought made his jealousy even more intense.

Dorek had once been a powerless prince fleeing like a defeated dog. Then Daniel appeared. With the support of that one extraordinary figure, Dorek had climbed step by step until he became one of the empire’s two recognized heirs.
Kane had never found an adviser capable of matching Daniel.
"I have raised nothing but useless trash! Every one of them is worthless!"
His furious curses echoed through the residence.

Across the Imperial City, countless powerful figures began joining Dorek or Alvin. At this stage, neutrality became increasingly difficult. Everyone understood that the capital could eventually contain only one ruler.
Experts who had supported the eliminated princes abandoned their former patrons and approached the two remaining factions.
More of them chose Dorek.
Alvin still attracted a large number of civil officials, but Dorek’s recent achievements, military authority, and Daniel’s terrifying reputation made his faction appear more likely to win.
Dorek did not become arrogant.
Daniel’s teaching had changed him. Even when he stood one step from supreme power, he remained cautious.
Inside his residence, Dorek looked toward Daniel with both anticipation and uncertainty.

"Teacher, Father is about to begin his tribulation. What should we do next? I am only one step away from the throne, yet the closer I come, the more frightened and confused I feel. I do not know which response is correct."
Daniel answered calmly.

"The matter is simple. Issue orders immediately. Send the imperial legions into the territories controlled by the major factions. Station troops in every important racial region and force those powers, along with the princes they supported, to declare loyalty to us."
Dorek listened in stunned silence.
Daniel continued.
"Then order every legion stationed outside the central territories to return toward the Imperial City and await further commands."
Dorek’s face changed completely.
The second instruction was even more shocking than the first. His hands began trembling.
"Teacher... are you suggesting a military uprising?"
Daniel’s plan appeared to use overwhelming force to seize the throne directly.
The possibility filled Dorek with fear. Power was a double-edged weapon. The closer he came to the imperial center, the more clearly he understood how easily one mistake could destroy him.
A failed military revolt would not merely end his political career. It would annihilate his faction, his allies, and perhaps the Fated Human Race supporting him.
Dorek swallowed.
"Is this not too impulsive? Should we consider the matter more carefully?"
Daniel smiled.
"You still have not understood the Eternal Emperor’s intention."
He leaned forward slightly.

"The Emperor needs an heir capable of ruthlessness. By selecting you and Alvin as two public successors at such a sensitive moment, he has placed you in a final contest. He is raising two candidates and forcing the stronger one to consume the other."
Daniel’s voice became colder.

"Tribulation-ash corruption is worsening throughout the universe. A kind and hesitant ruler cannot lead civilization through the coming disaster. Only a sovereign willing to make brutal decisions has the qualifications to inherit the empire."
He gestured toward Dorek.
"The Emperor gave you control of the legions as a test. You must learn to use the Strength in your hands to secure your own interests. If you refuse to act, Alvin will act first."
Dorek fell silent.
He considered the decree, the divided authority, and the crisis approaching the universe. Gradually, fear gave way to understanding.
He raised his head.
"I understand, Teacher. I will issue the military orders immediately."
A new fierceness appeared within him.
Daniel nodded in approval.
"Indecision creates chaos. Once a decision is required, hesitation becomes the greatest danger. Our chances of victory are high."
Dorek’s eyes brightened.
"What if Father had given us Alvin’s civil authority instead? How would we have competed then?"
Daniel considered the question briefly.

"That would also be simple. We would promise benefits, offices, and resources to the major officials and persuade powerful factions to join us. Once our political coalition reached sufficient scale, it could achieve the same objective."
Dorek finally understood.
Whether one held armies or administration, the essential principle remained the same.
Power had to be used before an opponent used theirs.

Even an existence at the peak of half-step Eternal could not escape the decline of the Great Dao.
Unless he completed his tribulation and broke through to the Eternal realm before the corruption consumed him, he would eventually lose himself and become a Tribulation-Ash Monster.
Only true Eternal power could transcend the decay of the universe.
Unfortunately, the Emperor had not chosen the timing of the tribulation.
It had descended upon him before he could complete all the preparations normally required for such an attempt.
His treasures, formations, and contingency plans were far from perfect.
Almost every major expert believed his chances of success were extremely small.
The Eternal Emperor himself apparently agreed.
In recent days, he had begun arranging matters that would take effect after his death.
The most urgent question was the selection of the next ruler.
He still had not named a single crown prince.
That did not surprise the political factions.
What surprised them was that, at the final moment, the Emperor appointed two princes to share the responsibilities normally held by one heir.
The first was Dorek.
According to the new decree, Prince Dorek would control every matter related to the imperial legions.
He received supreme authority over military appointments, deployments, and strategic commands.
The second was Prince Alvin.
Alvin would manage the empire’s civil administration and every major political matter unrelated to the legions.
The Eternal Emperor had divided the duties of a crown prince into two halves.
Military authority belonged to Dorek.
Civil authority belonged to Alvin.
The decree effectively eliminated every other prince from serious competition.
Only Dorek and Alvin retained the qualifications to fight for the throne.
Many experts found the arrangement dangerous.
Dividing civil and military power between rival heirs created an obvious risk that the empire itself would split into opposing camps.
Yet the Eternal Emperor had made the choice deliberately.
No one believed he had acted without purpose.
The entire Imperial City changed overnight.
Officials, noble clans, military families, and ancient factions began reevaluating their loyalties.
Those who had supported other princes felt their hearts sink.
Inside Prince Kane’s residence, expensive treasures shattered one after another.
Bang!
Bang!
Bang!
Kane hurled divine ornaments, ancient vessels, and priceless decorations against the floor.
"Damn it!
Why wasn’t I chosen?"
His hair hung loose around his face, and jealousy twisted his features.
"Why does Dorek control the military?
In what way am I inferior to him?
My cultivation, talent, and intelligence should all surpass his!
That position should belong to me.
I refuse to accept this!"
Beneath the rage lay fear.
Kane had previously dispatched experts to assassinate Dorek.
If Dorek became emperor, he would never forgive those attempts.
Kane could expect neither exile nor imprisonment.
His end would be complete destruction.
The thought made his jealousy even more intense.
Dorek had once been a powerless prince fleeing like a defeated dog.
Then Daniel appeared.
With the support of that one extraordinary figure, Dorek had climbed step by step until he became one of the empire’s two recognized heirs.
Kane had never found an adviser capable of matching Daniel.
"I have raised nothing but useless trash!
Every one of them is worthless!"
His furious curses echoed through the residence.
Across the Imperial City, countless powerful figures began joining Dorek or Alvin.
At this stage, neutrality became increasingly difficult.
Everyone understood that the capital could eventually contain only one ruler.
Experts who had supported the eliminated princes abandoned their former patrons and approached the two remaining factions.
More of them chose Dorek.
Alvin still attracted a large number of civil officials, but Dorek’s recent achievements, military authority, and Daniel’s terrifying reputation made his faction appear more likely to win.
Dorek did not become arrogant.
Daniel’s teaching had changed him.
Even when he stood one step from supreme power, he remained cautious.

What should we do next?
I am only one step away from the throne, yet the closer I come, the more frightened and confused I feel.
I do not know which response is correct."
Daniel answered calmly.
"The matter is simple.
Issue orders immediately.
Send the imperial legions into the territories controlled by the major factions.
Station troops in every important racial region and force those powers, along with the princes they supported, to declare loyalty to us."
Dorek listened in stunned silence.
Daniel continued.
"Then order every legion stationed outside the central territories to return toward the Imperial City and await further commands."
Dorek’s face changed completely.
The second instruction was even more shocking than the first.
His hands began trembling.
"Teacher... are you suggesting a military uprising?"
Daniel’s plan appeared to use overwhelming force to seize the throne directly.
The possibility filled Dorek with fear.
Power was a double-edged weapon.
The closer he came to the imperial center, the more clearly he understood how easily one mistake could destroy him.
A failed military revolt would not merely end his political career.
It would annihilate his faction, his allies, and perhaps the Fated Human Race supporting him.

Should we consider the matter more carefully?"
